finals.node_title: NODE 1 - Crude transfer from Repco separator V-301 (TP-04) and Test separator V-100 (TP-01A/B tie-in) through basket strainer ST-017 to Bullet Tank-C V-312, including V-312 vessel, level instruments, relief and atmospheric vent
finals.design_intent: Transfer separated crude under separator pressure (stated 7 barg, basis unconfirmed) from V-301 liquid outlet (downstream of LV-303, tie-in TP-04, 3"-PR-B013-8083-H) and from V-100 (tie-in TP-01A/B, 3"-PR-B013-8086-H, check valve + 3"-150# valve), both lined up at the same time (client answer 2), through single basket strainer L028-21-ST-017 (100% bypass 3"-PR-B013-8087-H, one valve LC at its inlet end, return leg unvalved) and 3"-PR-B013-8085-H into V-312 at N1 (TP-06A). V-312 is dedicated to hot oil operation (041 Note 4) and operates on the open atmospheric vent N10 -> 2",600# valve -> TP-08 2"-150# valve -> 2"-VF-B013-8095-X (about 3 m, HOLD 1) with the LAM-16 flare line closed (041 Note 5). All line-up is by manual valves; indication is by local gauges (PI-545, PI-54X, PI-543, PI-549, PI-550). The route by which well 192B reaches V-301 / V-100 (H1-25), the state of the well between batches (H1-26), the batch sequence (H1-28), fill rate, batch volume and V-312 working capacity (H1-05) are not yet provided. V-301 and V-100 internals are outside the node; their failures are recorded as causes only. Effects of hot return on V-312 are recorded in Node 2.

Where data are missing the row is ranked on the stated conservative basis. Environment ranked on the interim basis that a liquid release can reach the sea or uncontained ground (H1-31).

DP up to source pressure across basket of unknown collapse rating: basket failure releases debris to V-312, P-003 and heater coil. Operator opens LC bypass (unfiltered solids forward) or opens strainer mid-batch (see 17.1).

FIT-102C at LV-101B and FI-101 on 2"-PR-D013-3406-H (030); sheet reports '2 flow meters' and Barton chart/flow transmitter good - procedural only (readout/totaliser location not confirmed; does not see V-301 flow or the TP-02A/B route). 2. PSV-304A - NOT CREDITED (no certificate; does not protect the B013 section as such). 4. PSV-100B reported good - protects V-100 only. 5. PI-545, PI-543, PI-54X, PI-549 local - procedural. 6. 'Close upstream first' sequence - procedural, not yet written.

V-312 pressure rises above its (unknown) design pressure - possible loss of containment; the same pressure is imposed through open N1 / N4 / N6 on the new 150# attachments (8088-H, P-003 casing and seal, 8097-H, HOU hoses) - release at pump or HOU; large gas and crude-mist release from the 3 m vent and, if the TP-12 valve is open, at the V-001 tip and into V-001; cloud reaches HOU fired heater and diesel engine: flash fire / explosion with operators at tank, strainer and HOU. V-301 LSLL sensor (031: LSLL-305 on dedicated nozzles N15/N16, valves 142/143, separate from the LIC-302 / LG-301 standpipe on N18; sheet: LSLL-304) - hardware, NOT CREDITED (cable disconnected; no final element or logic drawn; chamber bottoms share a common line with the standpipe, H1-29). 2. LCP-002 - NOT CREDITED (never in service). 3. V-312 PSV - does not exist on 041. 4. 2" atmospheric vent - NOT CREDITED (capacity and dispersion not calculated, HOLD 1). 5. PI-549, PI-550 local - procedural, too slow; PG-1004 NOT CREDITED during filling (upstream of N6 valves). 6. LG-301 (good) - procedural. 7. HOU ESD / engine emergency air shut-off - NOT CREDITED (failed on test). 8. Gas detection - none shown.

HOLD on relief: no credit for R1-02 until R1-01 / R1-22 / R1-62 give a sized device and a named discharge route; flash-fire consequence stays at current until then. Further step to L3 conditional on LOPA (R1-54). H1-01, H1-03, H1-05, H1-08, H1-32. Low Level (10) cross-refers here.

rows.safeguards: 1. V-100 LSLL-101B, on one bridle (N4/N5) with LSHH-101B, LSH-101B and LG-102B - hardware, NOT CREDITED (no final element drawn, not on inspection sheet, common-cause blockage, no LCP for V-100). 2. Check valve on 8086-H - not a blow-by or overpressure barrier. 3. PSV-100B reported good - protects V-100 only. 4. V-100 level gauge - corroded (which of LG-102A/B not stated), NOT CREDITED. 5. Bypasses (019)/(020)/(005) - closed position procedural only. 6. V-312 PSV - none; 2" vent NOT CREDITED.

SAFETY CRITICAL defects: LV-102B, IA manifold, V-100 level gauge; LV-101B condition unknown and must be established. Residual: one step for the new LSLL trip only; HOLD on relief as 5.2. Which valve is on the route, what the switches do, whether 910091-010 is LV-101B: H1-12. H1-01, H1-03.

When the vent is then opened a slug of gas and liquid is thrown from the 3 m stack (reaction load on the stack).

PI-549 local - procedural; PI-550 is downstream of the TP-08 valve and does not read tank pressure if that valve is closed; PG-1004 reads the tank only when the N6 valves are open - NOT CREDITED during filling. 3. No pressure alarm. 4. Vent valve position control - procedural.

rows.consequences: Partial vacuum in V-312; vacuum rating unknown - possible shell buckling and subsequent leak.

rows.consequences: Hot surfaces and hot liquid at strainer and drains (burn injury during handling); contributes to thermal expansion of blocked sections (ranked in 5.7) and to hot back-flow (ranked in 3.2).

If the vent is restricted the tank goes liquid-full and takes feed pressure (5.4).

A trip valve at the tank end alone converts overfill into 5.1 / 1.2 and would earn no credit. Time to overfill and maximum fill level: H1-05, H1-07. PSD-232 logic: H1-09. Concurrent filling and heating: H1-28. Thermal swell is Node 2.

rows.consequences: Static discharge in a flammable vapour space: internal explosion or vent fire.

PI-54X on the outlet side inside the strainer block valves - placeholder tag, new, NOT CREDITED. 3. Single-valve isolation - not adequate against a 300#/600# source; no bleed between the strainer outlet valve / bypass return and the 3"-150# valve at V-312.

rows.consequences: Stem or body leak of gas / crude at separator pressure; seized stem (valve does not respond) or sheared stem; level gauge bolting failure releases liquid at operator height and removes a V-100 level indication.

rows.consequences: Relief path of running pumps elsewhere is blocked (overpressure of that equipment), or - if left open - those reliefs discharge into the batch and onto the 2" vent.

rows.safeguards: 1. None defined - no minimum manning, procedure, MOC or pre-start-up review presented.

recommendations.text: Issue an HP/LP interface and relief calculation (API 521) for the B013 section (8083/8085/8086/8087-H), ST-017, the line labelled B013 between TP-02A/B and TP-03, V-312 and the new 150# attachments on V-312 (8088-H, P-003, 8097-H, hoses), stating the maximum pressure at TP-04 and TP-01A/B from every connected source and covering blocked outlet, gas blow-by from V-301 and from V-100 (including instrument air failure), thermal expansion, fire and minimum metal temperature; issue before any hydrocarbon is introduced.

Install a code-compliant, non-isolable relief device on V-312, sized for the governing case from R1-01 and discharging to the LAM-16 flare header via N11 / 6"-VF-D013-6490-X (back-pressure and FSV-032 checked) or another closed system, unless the R1-62 study demonstrates that atmospheric discharge of the full relief rate is acceptable at the HOU, engine intake and manned positions; show it on P&ID 041.

Provide the logic and a dedicated fail-closed shutdown valve for the V-301 low-low level trip, the valve located on the C013 side of the spec break at TP-04 where the LV-303 bypass (017) cannot bypass it, independent of LIC-302 / LV-303 and not routed through LCP-002 unless the LCP is proven; function-test end to end with a signed record.

SAFETY CRITICAL defect: replace the V-301 low-low level switch on nozzles N15/N16 (031 tag LSLL-305; inspection sheet LSLL-304) as the sensor of the R1-03 trip, reconnect its cable and prove its set point by wet test.
SAFETY CRITICAL defect: replace the V-301 high-high level switch on nozzles N13/N14 (031 tag LSHH-304; inspection sheet LSHH-305), reconnect its cable and prove its set point by wet test.

finals.node_title: NODE 2 - Bullet Tank-C V-312 outlet (N4, TP-07) -> Hot Oil Unit Feed Pump P-003 with minimum-flow line 2"-PR-B013-8094-H -> Hot Oil Heater L028-68-H-001 (HOU feed pump P-001 bypassed) -> return 2"-PR-B013-8097-H to V-312 (recirculation / stabilisation) OR HP PD booster pump L028-68-P-002 -> chiksan -> hot oil header 2"-HD-D013-5128-X -> well flowlines (flushing)
finals.design_intent: Recirculation / stabilisation mode: draw crude from V-312 nozzle N4 ("NITROGEN CONN", TP-07) through 2"-PR-B013-8088-H (two 2"-150# valves with a 4" x 1000 mm leg and LOCAL DRAIN between them) to electric centrifugal pump P-003; deliver through 2"-PR-B013-8093-H (numbered 8048-H on sheet 062) to tie-in TP-10A/B on the existing 3" diesel feed line, through a hose and BV-001 into heater H-001; return heated crude from TP-11A/B through 2"-PR-B013-8097-H (PI-551, TI-527) and TP-05 to V-312 top nozzle N6, heating the tank contents and liberating gas to the atmospheric vent (041 Note 5, 062 Note 4). Pump protected by minimum recirculation line 8094-H returning to the V-312 inlet line 8085-H (041 Note 3). Flushing mode: once the crude is stabilised, heater outlet is lined through the 2" valve at TP-11 to PD pump P-002 and via chiksan pipe (single 2",600# check valve and valve), 2"-DF-D013-XXX-X and header 2"-HD-D013-5128-X into the flowlines 4"-PR-D013-087/089/090/092/093/094-X of wells 120, 134LS/SS, 136LS/SS, 137LS/SS through single small-bore (1", and 1/2" "HOT OIL" at well 120) valves; no check valve is identified at any injection point on 062; the header continues to 2"-HD-D013-6079-H "TO FLOW LINE SLOT-01 & 02". Intent is to do this without loss of containment, without firing the heater on low/no flow, without exceeding the heater outlet temperature limit and without releasing a flammable cloud that can reach the HOU burner or engine. Flow, batch volume, temperatures, fill/heat/flush/refill sequence and stabilisation criterion are not yet defined (HOLD H2-01, H2-04, H2-06, H2-30).

rows.remarks: HOLD H2-08, H2-15, H2-24. Residual = current.

rows.cause: Low coil outlet pressure by design: heater outlet discharges through open 2" line 8097-H to a top nozzle of an atmospherically vented tank with no back-pressure device; crude drawn from the open-vented heated tank is at bubble point and flashes in the coil and in 8097-H as it is heated (normal operation, nothing failed).
rows.consequences: Vapour blanketing and high film temperature in the coil at full flow (coking, tube hot spots, eventual coil leak and heater fire); slug flow and vibration in the 2" line and hose; erratic flow that can chatter or defeat a low-flow switch.
rows.safeguards: 1. None - no back-pressure control, no coil skin or film temperature indication. 2. PI-551, TI-527 local (procedural).
rows.remarks: Added on Process challenge. HOLD H2-32 (vendor film temperature / minimum velocity), H2-01, H2-06. Residual = current (study action).

rows.cause: V-312 pumped down in flushing mode or cooling after a hot batch on the open atmospheric vent (or with vent closed). N4, labelled nitrogen connection, is used as pump suction - no inerting shown.
rows.consequences: Open vent: air drawn into warm hydrocarbon vapour space - flammable mixture inside V-312 for next heat-up; internal explosion if ignited (see 15). Closed vent: vacuum on vessel of unknown vacuum rating.
rows.safeguards: 1. Open vent if lined up (procedural). 2. No vacuum relief, no blanketing.
rows.remarks: HOLD H2-02 (vacuum rating), H2-09 (nitrogen availability). Residual = current. Same hazard recorded in Node 1 for the fill phase; this row covers pump-out/cool-down.

rows.cause: Feed HOSE (or its couplings) between the 3" line and the heater bursts or separates; loss of heater inlet pressure not detected.
rows.consequences: Crude at pump discharge pressure, hot on recirculation, sprayed beside burner and engine; burner continues to fire on a starved coil; spray/pool fire at manned unit.
rows.safeguards: 1. HOU Murphy low-pressure switch (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, frozen reading; what it senses unconfirmed (may be an engine device); a usable trip point between normal low back-pressure and burst is not shown to exist. 2. Hose certification/test (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, none presented. 3. Burner ESD (hardware) - NOT CREDITED.
rows.remarks: Residual credits R2-36 (certified hose / designed flexible element) only; HOLD H2-07 / H2-31 for any credit to the low-pressure switch, which stays SAFETY CRITICAL if it is the process loss-of-feed trip. H2-15 hose data.

rows.cause: Burner over-firing: outlet temperature control not shown (manual throttle), low coil flow, operator fires harder to shorten stabilisation, speed regulator malfunction (function unknown - may affect firing); frozen high-temperature gauge shows a static 'ideal' value.
rows.consequences: Crude above the 75-80 degC of 062 Note 5 returns to V-312: violent gas evolution; if a water heel is present and its boiling point is passed, steam flashing and froth-over of hot crude from the 3 m vent onto the HOU area - burns, pool fire; coking and coil failure; unknown design temperature of V-312, B013, hose, pump seal exceeded.
rows.safeguards: 1. HOU Murphy high-temperature switch (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, defective; whether it senses heater outlet or an engine temperature is unknown. 2. TIA-1003 on V-312 (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, LOW alarm only drawn, bulk temperature only, condition not reported. 3. TI-527 local on return (procedural, new; bypassed in flushing mode). 4. HOU temperature gauges (procedural) - NOT CREDITED until calibrated. 5. Alarm bypass switch non-functional - alarm integrity unknown.
rows.remarks: High-temperature switch SAFETY CRITICAL. One step only, for the new heater-outlet trip R2-29; HOLD H2-31 (what the Murphy switch senses), H2-01 (confirmed temperatures), H2-05 and H2-27 (water heel cannot yet be drawn off). Trip set point cannot be fixed until R2-30 is answered.

rows.cause: Normal intent of recirculation mode: hot return enters top nozzle N6 and flashes in the vapour space; gas rate set by heater duty and crude GOR with no limit, for the whole stabilisation period of every batch.
rows.consequences: Sustained hydrocarbon vapour release from a 2" vent about 3 m above grade, shared with open drain tank / V-001 vent; heavier-than-air vapour and mist reach the fired heater, diesel engine, P-003 motor and LCPs - flash fire with crew in the cloud; vapour pushed into V-001 and open drains.
rows.safeguards: 1. 'Vent to atmosphere at safe location' (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, height/location on HOLD 1, dispersion not done. 2. Gas detection - none shown. 3. HOU ESD / engine air shut-off (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, failed. 4. Client statement no H2S.
rows.remarks: HOLD H2-03, H2-06, H2-18. Likelihood 5 on challenge: release is intended and continuous, every layer dead as found. Residual = current: NO HEATING ON CRUDE until HOLD 1 is closed. If the flare route (R2-65) is adopted, re-rank with likelihood reduced; if not, R2-27 must demonstrate no flammable concentration at the HOU burner and engine intake at the maximum evolution rate from R2-26.

rows.cause: Normal hot operation: uninsulated hot items (hoses, pump casing, valves, flanges, chiksan, '-X' vent line 8095-X, V-312 shell and existing N6 header - insulation status not shown) and thermal growth / skid vibration on lines between fixed points (V-312 nozzles N4/N6, P-003, HOU skid).
rows.consequences: Contact burns; expansion and vibration loads on small ex-stock pump nozzles, vessel nozzles, skid nozzle / BV-001 and small-bore branches (PI-551, TI-527 thermowell) - misalignment, seal or flange leak.
rows.safeguards: 1. '-H' lines insulated/traced (hardware) - partial, hoses and pump not covered. 2. No flexibility check referenced. 3. PPE (procedural).
rows.remarks: Asset residual = current pending flexibility check result (H2-24). H2-26 (insulation of existing equipment).

rows.cause: Hot crude in the existing common level bridle (N7A/N7B, 2",300# LO valves) and LG-1004 gauge glass, where the operator reads level at fixed intervals; gauge glass type, temperature rating and excess-flow checks unknown; N7B carries the label 'HOT INLET/OUTLET' on 041.
rows.consequences: Gauge glass or bridle leak of hot crude at the reading position: burns to the operator, spill at the tank, possible fire.
rows.safeguards: 1. N7A/N7B isolation valves (procedural). 2. Gauge glass rating / ball checks - NOT CREDITED, unknown. 3. PPE (procedural).
rows.remarks: Added on HSE challenge. HOLD H2-26, H2-11 (meaning of 'HOT INLET/OUTLET' at N7B). Residual = current until answered.

rows.cause: Burner flame-out or trip not noticed (status lamps defective), followed by relight attempt; flame reset button damaged; repeated manual relight is the expected behaviour as found.
rows.consequences: Unburnt fuel accumulates in firebox; relight without purge - firebox explosion at the burner panel.
rows.safeguards: 1. Flame detection / fuel shut-off / purge logic (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, unknown. 2. Flame reset button (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, mechanically damaged. 3. Ignitor switch working (procedural).
rows.remarks: Flame reset SAFETY CRITICAL as part of burner sequence. Likelihood raised to 4 on challenge (no working protection as found). HOLD H2-07: flame failure protection unknown - residual = current.

rows.cause: Crude cools in 2" lines, hoses, pump and coil between batches or after burner trip (hoses and 3" DF line not traced); flushing started before tank reaches temperature. No means of displacing crude from coil, hoses and pump is defined; the diesel supply is the only displacement fluid shown and R2-22 isolates it.
rows.consequences: Wax/gel plug: dead-head on restart, operators break flanges or apply external heat; cold crude to flowlines gives no flushing benefit.
rows.safeguards: 1. Heat tracing on -H lines (hardware) - status unproven, NOT CREDITED until commissioned. 2. TI-527; TIA-1003 low alarm (annunciation point unconfirmed) (procedural).
rows.remarks: HOLD H2-28 (end-of-batch displacement method and return to diesel service), H2-05 (WAT/pour point), H2-17. Residual = current on challenge: a procedure without a displacement method is not a reduction.

rows.cause: Thermal expansion, gas swell and foaming of V-312 contents during heating after filling near H 2000 mm; or continued inflow during recirculation (Node 1 feed open, including live make-up into the hot tank; V-001 pump P-116A/B via 7917; passing inlets; LCV-1005 FO).
rows.consequences: Hot crude and foam (up to 75-80 degC per 062 Note 5) ejected from the 3 m vent and into open drain tank / V-001 with the burner firing: scalding spray on personnel required at tank and HOU, pool fire near HOU, spill.
rows.safeguards: 1. LSHH-1004 / PSD-232 (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, action unknown, untested, switch type unknown and may not see foam. 2. LT-1004 / LG-1004 on same bridle (procedural) - condition not reported. 3. No knock-out on vent.
rows.remarks: People raised to C on challenge, consistent with Node 1 cold overfill from the same vent. One step only (fill limit R2-32 + burner trip R2-33); no severity credit until the R2-63 mitigation is designed. Stopping the burner does not stop inflow - Node 1 fill shutdown on the same PSD-232 is required. HOLD H2-04, H2-11 (switch type / foam), H2-30. Cold overfill during filling is ranked in Node 1.

rows.cause: V-312 pumped down in flushing mode with no make-up (or lost through open outlet/drain, see dev 4 BV-358/359), nobody at LG-1004; bridle plugged with wax; suction nozzle N4 uncovers. N4 is drawn on the head near N13 level, apart from the bottom nozzles; its elevation relative to L 400 / LL 300 mm is unknown.
rows.consequences: P-003 loses suction and coil flow stops with burner firing - escalates to heater fire (first row of dev 1); pump damage; P-002 starved; air drawn into tank; TT-1003 reads vapour.
rows.safeguards: 1. LSLL-1004 / PSD-231 at 300 mm (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, final element not shown, no link to P-003 or burner, untested, legacy setting may be below N4, shares bridle with LG/LT. 2. HOU low-flow switch (hardware) - NOT CREDITED. 3. LG-1004, LT-1004 L 400 mm (procedural) - readout/alarm location unconfirmed.
rows.remarks: Residual limited to one step on challenge: HOLD H2-09 (N4 elevation vs trip level), H2-11 (PSD-231 existing actions, common bridle). V-312 level instruments become safety critical and are unverified.

rows.cause: Free water heel and sand/solids in V-312 bottom and in the 4" suction leg drawn into P-003 and the heater (water from separators/LLP header; solids if ST-017 was bypassed). The heel below N4 cannot be removed by the N4 leg drain.
rows.consequences: Water slugs flash in the coil: pressure surges, hose whip; steam/froth in tank (ranked under 7); sand erodes pump seal and settles in coil causing hot spots and coil leak.
rows.safeguards: 1. LOCAL DRAIN on N4 leg (procedural) - does not drain the tank heel. 2. Tank bottom draw-off route - NOT CREDITED, not defined (bottom outlets are the NC BV-358 / BV-359 routes into other systems). 3. Suction strainer (hardware) - mesh unknown, no DP indication. 4. No water or interface detection on V-312.
rows.remarks: HOLD H2-27 (water draw-off nozzle, route, destination), H2-05 (water cut, sand), H2-23. Residual = current until the draw-off route is defined (R2-61); R2-31 hold point cannot be performed before that.

rows.cause: Crude declared 'stabilised' without a defined criterion; residual dissolved gas; residual diesel in HOU/hoses mixed with crude.
rows.consequences: Gas breakout at P-002 suction and in the flush (vapour lock, pulsation); continued gas release where flush returns arrive; mixture of unknown flash point at vent.
rows.safeguards: 1. None instrumented. 2. No sample point shown on new lines.
rows.remarks: HOLD H2-06, H2-29 (where flush returns go).

rows.cause: Burner light-off with flame reset damaged, alarm bypass switch non-functional (bypass state unknown), LCP internals extensively corroded and status lamps dead; burner lit before flow is proven; operators improvise (jumpers, repeated attempts).
rows.consequences: Unburnt-fuel light-off explosion in firebox; heater run with trips permanently bypassed; coil overheated at start.
rows.safeguards: 1. Flame reset (hardware) - NOT CREDITED. 2. Alarm bypass switch (hardware) - NOT CREDITED. 3. Burner LCP (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, corroded. 4. Ignitor, throttle and burner start/stop/run switches working (procedural). 5. BMS / purge logic - NOT CREDITED, unknown.
rows.remarks: Flame reset, alarm bypass switch and burner LCP internals are SAFETY CRITICAL. Likelihood 4 on challenge. Residual one step only; HOLD H2-07 - further reduction only when R2-52 confirms a flame-failure fuel shut-off and purge sequence exists.

rows.cause: Emergency at HOU or vent (hose burst, coil leak, gas cloud) needing immediate shutdown: burner LCP ESD button destroyed; emergency air shut-off valve does not respond to ESD from burner or engine LCP; whether ESD also shuts burner fuel is unknown; P-003 stop is at its own LCP by V-312; no remote isolation at tank outlet N4; separators may still be feeding V-312 (Node 1).
rows.consequences: Burner and engine keep running in a gas cloud, P-003 keeps feeding the leak and V-312 inventory gravity-feeds it through N4 / 8088-H; operator must approach the engine to close the air valve manually - escalation to major fire, multiple casualties, loss of HOU and V-312.
rows.safeguards: 1. Burner ESD button (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, inoperable. 2. Emergency air shut-off on ESD, both LCPs (hardware) - NOT CREDITED. 3. Local manual air shut-off (procedural) - requires approach to hazard, NOT CREDITED as emergency protection. 4. No defined escape route, muster point or alarm means for the crew between vent and heater.
rows.remarks: ESD button and emergency air shut-off are SAFETY CRITICAL - mitigation layer for most Node 2 scenarios. Residual valid only with the N4 remote isolation (R2-64) and the common ESD (R2-46) installed; otherwise residual = current. HOLD H2-31 (ESD cause-and-effect), H2-18 (link to platform ESD/F&G).

rows.cause: First crude service of untested new lines 8088/8093/8094/8097-H and tie-ins TP-05, TP-07, TP-10, TP-11, ex-stock pump P-003, and existing coil/hoses previously on diesel.
rows.consequences: Leak at new joint, hose coupling or pump seal on first pressurisation/heat-up; crude release at the manned fired unit, fire.
rows.safeguards: 1. None documented - no test, flushing or commissioning record.
rows.remarks: People raised to C on challenge (same outcome as hose-burst row). Residual held at one step; a second step is available once signed test records exist, including a coil test at a documented pressure (H2-07). H2-25 (test/PSSR plan, MOC).

rows.cause: Electrical power failure stops P-003 while the self-contained engine/burner unit (and P-002 in flushing mode) keeps running.
rows.consequences: Heater fired with no flow - recorded and ranked once under 1. No / Less Flow (first row).
rows.safeguards: As 1. No / Less Flow first row: no interlock P-003 to burner; low-flow switch NOT CREDITED.
rows.remarks: Cross-reference only, not ranked twice.

rows.cause: Loss of HOU air / charge pressure or control power in the corroded burner LCP; air and charge pressure gauges non-functional so the state cannot be seen.
rows.consequences: Burner fuel valve and shutdown devices in an unknown state; loss of burner control or failure to trip; engine distress unannounced.
rows.safeguards: 1. Air / charge pressure gauges, engine LCP air gauge (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, non-functional. 2. Status lamps (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, defective. 3. Fail action of fuel valve on air loss - unknown.
rows.remarks: H2-07 (fail-safe action of burner fuel valve).

rows.cause: Repeated sampling of hot crude from drains or gauge bleeds to judge stabilisation and water content; no sample point or method defined.
rows.consequences: Hot volatile crude to an open container: burns, vapour flash, static ignition of sample, small spill.
rows.safeguards: 1. None shown. 2. PPE (procedural).

rows.cause: Operator decisions taken on false indication: HOU low-pressure and high-temperature gauges show a static 'ideal' value running or stopped; other T/P gauges uncalibrated.
rows.consequences: Over-temperature or loss of feed not recognised; crude declared ready when it is not; delayed response to all heater upsets.
rows.safeguards: 1. TI-527, PI-551 new local instruments (procedural). 2. HOU T/P gauges (procedural) - NOT CREDITED until calibrated.
rows.remarks: Enabler for 1 and 7; ranked for its own direct effect only.

rows.cause: Hot return through top nozzle N6 falls through the vapour space (splash, mist, charge) when air may be present (dev 6); unbonded or non-conductive hoses and new spools.
rows.consequences: Static discharge in a flammable vapour space: internal explosion of V-312 or vent fire with operators at tank and pump.
rows.safeguards: 1. None shown: no inerting, no dip pipe, no bonding detail, vent tip device type not stated.
rows.remarks: HOLD H2-09, H2-03 (vent tip), H2-15 (hose conductivity). Residual = current pending inerting/return decision.

rows.cause: Vapour from the vent, a seal or hose leak reaches the HOU: burner is a continuous ignition source, diesel engine ingests vapour at its air intake; hot exhaust / firebox surfaces; corroded LCP wiring; P-003 motor/LCP Ex rating unknown.
rows.consequences: Engine overspeed/runaway (no longer controlled by fuel), ignition of cloud, flash fire at the unit.
rows.safeguards: 1. Emergency air shut-off valve (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, does not respond to ESD on either LCP, manual only; automatic overspeed actuation not stated. 2. ESD button (hardware) - NOT CREDITED. 3. Gas detection - none shown. 4. Separation distance / hazardous area drawing - not provided.
rows.remarks: Emergency air shut-off SAFETY CRITICAL. Residual limited to one step on challenge and conditional on R2-28 having executive action and R2-62 fitted; the release itself (dev 7, second row) remains at current risk. H2-18 (layout, Ex rating, overspeed trip, intake location).

rows.cause: Draining the N4 drop leg ('LOCAL DRAIN', no destination), pump 3/4" drains, hoses and coil at end of batch while hot; drains left cracked open or uncapped.
rows.consequences: Hot crude/oily water to grade at pump and under fired equipment; burns; spill.
rows.safeguards: 1. Single drain valves, no caps, destination 'local' (procedural).
rows.remarks: H2-21 (drain destinations, containment), H2-28.

rows.cause: Connecting/disconnecting hoses and chiksan between diesel and crude service, between campaigns and modes.
rows.consequences: Residual hot crude released at a broken connection; wrong hose reconnected (heater bypassed).
rows.safeguards: 1. Manual valves, no bleeds on hose sections (procedural).
rows.remarks: Hose burst in service is ranked under 6 (third row). H2-28 (return to diesel service).

rows.cause: Work on P-003 seal or suction strainer. Tank side has two 2"-150# block valves (at N4 / TP-07 and near the pump) with the 4" leg LOCAL DRAIN between them as bleed; the HOU side (check valve + 2"-150# valve on 8093-H) and the minimum-flow side (check valve + valve on 8094-H) are single valve plus check with no bleed. No standby pump; tag conflict (symbol L028-21-P-003, data box L028-68-P-003) and line number conflict (8093-H on 041, 8048-H on 062).
rows.consequences: Hot crude release through a passing discharge-side valve onto the technician; wrong equipment isolated.
rows.safeguards: 1. Double block and bleed available on suction side (procedural). 2. 3/4" drains for zero-energy check (procedural). 3. Single isolation plus check on discharge and minimum-flow sides.
rows.remarks: Isolation description corrected on Mechanical challenge (verified on 041). H2-22.

rows.cause: Panel refurbishment and field rewiring of low-flow switch, flame reset, ESD and switches: wiring errors or trips left disconnected/bypassed after work.
rows.consequences: Trips believed restored do not act on burner fuel - heater scenarios proceed unprotected.
rows.safeguards: 1. None formal - no return-to-service test requirement stated.
rows.remarks: Controls the validity of every residual ranking that credits a restored HOU trip.

rows.cause: Heater coil condition unknown (no thickness or pressure test record; design pressure, temperature and material unknown); service change from diesel to crude with possible water, salts and sand; coke/scale; extensive corrosion already found inside burner LCP.
rows.consequences: Coil leak into firebox - heater fire; loss of protection through corroded terminals (see 12).
rows.safeguards: 1. Coil inspection record (hardware) - NOT CREDITED, none. 2. ST-017 upstream when not bypassed (hardware) - mesh unknown.
rows.remarks: Residual limited to one step on challenge: one test does not control in-service fouling, coking or erosion, and the test pressure cannot be set without coil data - HOLD H2-07.

rows.cause: P-003 mechanical seal or casing joint leak in normal running: ex-stock pump with aged elastomers, seal type unknown, hot volatile crude (75-80 degC per 062 Note 5) near bubble point, sand.
rows.consequences: Hot crude spray or pool at the pump beside V-312, with motor and LCP of unknown Ex rating; fire under V-312 with operator at the pump LCP.
rows.safeguards: 1. None evidenced - no seal specification, no drip containment, no leak detection.
rows.remarks: Added on Mechanical challenge. Residual valid only when the new seal is confirmed suitable for the service - HOLD H2-08. Seal failure caused by cavitation / dead-head is under dev 1.

rows.cause: Long recirculation treated like the old diesel job: HOU and V-312 left unattended or run at night with non-functional work lights and no remote indication of level, temperature or pressure.
rows.consequences: Any deviation above (flame-out, over-temperature, vent carry-over, low level) develops with nobody present and no working trip.
rows.safeguards: 1. None - HOU protections defective; work light / toolbox light switches non-functional.
rows.remarks: H2-20 (manning, night operation).

rows.cause: Volatile crude replaces diesel in a unit, layout and emergency arrangement set up for diesel: operators stand at burner/engine panels, pump LCP and tank gauges inside the potential vapour zone; no hazardous area, F&G, fire-fighting or escape information; fire under V-312 holding hot crude with no PSV.
rows.consequences: A leak that was a nuisance on diesel becomes a fire on crude; fire exposure of V-312 with only the 2" vent; escape route may pass vent or heater.
rows.safeguards: 1. None demonstrated on any document provided.
rows.remarks: HOLD H2-18, H2-02. Residual = current until area classification and fire-case relief (Node 1) are resolved.

recommendations.text: SAFETY CRITICAL: replace the damaged HOU heater low-flow switch and rewire it, confirm it senses flow in the path used with P-001 bypassed (downstream of the BV-001 entry), and prove by witnessed test that it shuts off burner fuel at the set point issued from R2-60; no firing on crude before the signed test record exists.

SAFETY CRITICAL: replace the defective HOU Murphy high-temperature switch/gauge, confirm that it senses heater outlet temperature, and prove by witnessed test that it trips burner fuel at the set point issued by Process Engineering.

SAFETY CRITICAL: replace the defective HOU Murphy low-pressure switch/gauge, confirm what it senses, and prove by test that it trips the burner at the set point issued by Process Engineering (if no usable trip point exists in recirculation mode, record that loss of feed is covered by R2-54 only).
SAFETY CRITICAL: replace the destroyed ESD push button on the burner LCP and prove by witnessed test that it shuts burner fuel and closes the engine air shut-off valve.
SAFETY CRITICAL: rectify the emergency air shut-off valve so that it closes on the ESD signal from both the burner LCP and the engine LCP, and record a witnessed closure test from each panel.
SAFETY CRITICAL: replace the damaged flame reset button with complete field rewiring and function-test the burner reset/relight sequence.
SAFETY CRITICAL: replace the non-functional alarm bypass switch and prove that every alarm and trip is live with the switch in the normal position.

SAFETY CRITICAL: refurbish the corroded burner LCP internals (components, terminals, cabling) and loop-test every trip from sensor to burner fuel shut-off, witnessed by Operations, with a signed return-to-service sheet.

SAFETY CRITICAL (until the function of each regulator and the P-002 relief valve are confirmed): replace both malfunctioning HOU speed regulators and carry out a full functional check of each controlled drive.
Replace the non-functional air pressure and charge pressure gauges, the engine LCP air pressure gauge and the defective status lamps (charging, low oil pressure, coolant overheat, glow plug).
Calibrate the HOU temperature and pressure gauges and the new TI-527 and PI-551, with certificates, before the trial.
Replace the non-functional work light and toolbox light switches on the engine LCP.
Inspect, flush the common bridle of, and function-test LSHH-1004, LSLL-1004, LT-1004, LG-1004, TT/TIA-1003 and PG-1004 on V-312, and issue the test record (no inspection sheet exists).

Connect LSLL-1004 / PSD-231 to trip burner fuel and stop P-003 through a hard-wired trip input on the P-003 starter (with run-status contact), with the trip level set from the R2-17 result and N4 elevation (do not reuse 300 mm by default), and function-test end to end.
Provide a hard-wired trip of burner fuel and of P-002 on P-003 not running, function-tested.
Install a restriction orifice sized for P-003 minimum continuous flow in 2"-PR-B013-8094-H, with its manual valve locked open and shown so on the P&ID.

Issue an NPSH and suction line sizing calculation for P-003 at maximum crude temperature and minimum V-312 level using the actual N4 elevation, pump NPSHr and nozzle sizes (reducer eccentric, flat side up), and state the minimum operating / trip level and the usable batch volume between maximum pre-heat level and the trip.

Obtain the P-003 data sheet and curve (rated point, shut-off head, minimum flow, actual nozzle sizes, casing rating, seal type, maximum temperature, motor power and Ex certificate) and confirm shut-off pressure is below the lowest-rated component.

Complete an HP/LP interface review of every low-pressure side of P-002 and of TP-05 against the maximum flowline, P-002 discharge and 5037-X pressures (2" at TP-11 and 8097-H, BTV-002/003 manifold and hose, 3" DF line, 8093/8048-H, heater coil, diesel supply, hoses, V-312), and specify the protection to be installed.
Install a check valve on 2"-PR-B013-8097-H at TP-11B.
State in the flushing procedure that the 2"-150# return valve at TP-11 is closed and locked before any injection valve is opened, and injection / header valves are closed before P-002 is stopped.

Positively isolate (spade or remove spool) the diesel supply at the 3" valve at TP-10A for the crude campaign and enter it on the isolation register, once the end-of-batch displacement fluid is named under H2-28.

Positively isolate the branch to the filter pot / pump P-001 (including the P-001 discharge connection to the heater) and disconnect the second hose to BTV-002/003 for the crude campaign, recorded on the isolation register.

Confirm the duty of 2"-PR-D013-5037-X (LCV-1005, recycle/PSV) and 3"-PR-B013-5094-X during the campaign and, where confirmed not a relief path, lock their isolation valves closed on the lock register.

Confirm the existence, set pressure, test date and discharge destination of the heater coil relief valve and the P-002 discharge relief valve (P-002 relief set at or below the lowest-rated item downstream: chiksan, 2"-DF/HD-D013 header, flowlines), and report any that is missing for installation before firing.

Include the Node 2 cases (gas evolution at maximum heater duty, heat input with vent restricted, live feed admitted to the hot tank, reverse flow from flowlines) in the V-312 relief and vent sizing calculation raised in Node 1.

Complete the HOLD 1 dispersion calculation for stabilisation gas at the maximum evolution rate, liquid carry-over and the shared open drain tank / V-001 vent, with the HOU burner, engine air intake and manned positions as receptors, and fix vent height and location from it.
Provide gas detection at the HOU burner and engine air intake with alarm at the manned point and executive action (burner fuel shut-off, engine air shut-off, P-003 stop).
Install an independent high-high temperature trip with high alarm on the heater outlet at TP-11A/B, upstream of the mode valves, hard-wired to burner fuel shut-off and function-tested.

Issue the maximum heater outlet temperature, V-312 bulk temperature and heat-up rate / burner duty during stabilisation, checked against water content and the design temperatures of V-312, B013 piping, hoses and the P-003 seal.
Make draw-off of free water from V-312 (by the route defined under R2-61) and from the suction leg, confirmed by sample, a signed hold point before the heater is lit.
Calculate and issue the maximum pre-heat fill level of V-312 allowing for thermal expansion and foaming.
Configure LSHH-1004 / PSD-232 as one cause-and-effect entry common to both nodes - trip burner fuel (P-003 keeps circulating) together with the Node 1 fill shutdown - and function-test it.

Issue the Node 2 operating procedure with a valve-by-valve matrix for recirculation, flushing and change-over (open new route before closing old), Node 1 inlet 3"-150# valve closed and tagged before light-off unless make-up is specifically designed for, flow proven before light-off, the manual sequence on a P-003 stop (burner off, P-002 stopped, injection valve closed), post-firing circulation, an open path to V-312 after shutdown, the end-of-batch displacement step (per H2-28), a ban on external heating or breaking flanges on a suspected wax plug without a permit, and independent check of each line-up.
Define the stabilisation end-point test and the minimum temperature permissive for change-over to flushing, as a supervisor-signed hold point.

challenges.challenge: On 030 the new tie between TP-02A/B (LV-102B outlet, 2"-PR-D013-106-H) and TP-03 (LLP header 4"-PR-D013-5076-X) is labelled 3"-PR-B013-8087-H. challenges.row_ref: 4.2 Other V-312 inlet left open / 3.3 TP-09
challenges.challenge: The TP-09 valve separates nozzle N10 from the existing line to the fuel gas conditioning skid (049). N10 is the only vent in use, and V-312 will breathe air through it (row 6.2). If the TP-09 valve is open or passes, an air/hydrocarbon mixture reaches the fuel gas system, or fuel gas feeds the 3 m vent. R1-19's blind list does not include this line. R1-22 only asks for it to be included in a calculation.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING
challenges.challenge: The worksheet assumes V-301 receives only cold well 192B fluid. 031 Note 2 reads 'Repco separator shall be dedicated for hot oil unit operation, during heating of stabilized crude oil from flushing operation'. On 062 the hot crude is injected into flowlines downstream of the chokes. The flush fluid, with dislodged wax and solids at up to the heater temperature, may therefore return through the production header to V-301 and back to ST-017 and V-312 as a closed loop. That would change the strainer loading (1.1), the operating temperature of V-301 and the B013 lines (7.1), and the batch balance (9.1).
challenges.proposed_change: Add a parking-lot item to Client / Operations: 'Where do the flushed flowlines discharge during flushing? Is the returned hot flush fluid routed to V-301 or V-100 and re-circulated to V-312? Maximum return temperature and wax/solids load?' It affects rows 1.1, 7.1 and 9.1. Interim basis: return to V-301 is credible. Add 'wax/solids slug from flushed flowlines' to the 1.1 cause.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING
challenges.challenge: There is no row for vaporisation in the coil and return line in normal operation. The heater outlet discharges through an open 2" line (8097-H) to a top nozzle of an atmospherically vented tank, with no back-pressure device. P-003 offers only 34 m differential head per the data box. Crude drawn from an open-vented heated tank is at its bubble point, so it flashes inside the coil and in 8097-H as it is heated. This gives vapour blanketing and high film temperature (coking, tube hot spots) at full flow. It also gives slug flow and vibration in the 2" line and hose, and erratic flow that can chatter or defeat a low-flow switch. None of the existing rows covers it, because nothing has failed.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a row under 6 Low Pressure: 'Low coil outlet pressure by design - no back-pressure on heater outlet; crude at bubble point flashes in coil and 8097-H'. Safeguards: none. Rank People C4 / Env E4 / Asset D4 / Rep D4, residual = current, HOLD. New recommendation (Process Engineering, before start-up): calculate vapour fraction and film temperature in the coil at the intended outlet temperature and pressure, and specify the minimum coil outlet pressure and how it is held (restriction or back-pressure valve at the V-312 end of 8097-H, upstream of relief considerations). New parking-lot item to the HOU vendor: maximum film temperature and minimum coil velocity for crude service.

challenges.row_ref: 2 More Flow - minimum-flow line fully open (and 1 No/Less Flow first row)
challenges.challenge: The row is ranked asset-only (People NA), yet its consequence is coil flow below what the heater needs while the burner fires. That is the same coil-overheat outcome as the first No/Less Flow row, and here it can occur by design, not by failure. The HOU's own feed pump P-001 is bypassed. P-003 is an ex-stock pump with 34 m head that must push through hoses, the coil (pressure drop unknown) and up to N6, while an unrestricted 2" recycle (8094-H) is in parallel. Nobody has shown that P-003 can deliver the heater's minimum flow. The location of the HOU 'heater low flow' switch relative to the BV-001 entry is also unknown. If it sits on the P-001 side it is bypassed along with P-001, and R2-01 restores a switch that sees nothing.
challenges.proposed_change: Move the cause to 1 No/Less Flow as 'insufficient coil flow by design / recycle split', ranked People C4 / Env E4 / Asset D4 / Rep D4. Residual C3 with R2-16 and R2-54. Add a recommendation (Process Engineering, before start-up): system curve for P-003 through the coil to N6 against the heater's minimum flow, with the coil pressure drop from the vendor. Amend R2-01: 'confirm the switch senses flow in the path used with P-001 bypassed (downstream of BV-001); if not, install a new low-flow trip on the heater feed 8093/8048-H'. Add both questions to H2-07.

challenges.row_ref: 3 Reverse Flow - P-002 stops with wells lined up
challenges.challenge: Three drawing facts on 062 are missing or wrong. (1) Injection is not into the wells. The chiksan feeds 2"-DF-D013-XXX-X and then header 2"-HD-D013-5128-X, which connects by single 1" valves (1/2" 'HOT OIL' at well 120) to the flowlines 4"-PR-D013-087/089/090/092/093/094-X downstream of the chokes. The header also continues to 'FLOW LINE SLOT-01 & 02' (2"-HD-D013-6079-H). No check valve is drawn at any injection point, so the single 2",600# check at the chiksan is the only non-return device. (2) P-002 has a second low-pressure connection: BTV-002/BTV-003 4" manifold, 4"x3" reducer, 3" valve and hose back to the 3" feed line at TP-10B. A stopped PD pump passing back therefore pressurises that hose, the heater inlet, the P-003 discharge (B013) and the diesel supply 3"-DF-B013-XXX-X, not only the TP-11 tee. (3) Header 5128-X cross-connects seven flowlines through single valves.
challenges.proposed_change: Correct the design intent and row text to 'flowlines via 2"-HD-D013-5128-X; single 1" valve, no NRV at each injection point'. Add the BTV-002/003 hose route to the cause. Add the consequence 'cross-flow between flowlines through 5128-X with two injection valves open or passing'. Extend R2-19 to every low-pressure side of P-002: the 2" at TP-11, the BTV manifold and hose, the 3" DF line, 8093/8048-H, the heater coil and the diesel supply. Replace the NRV question in H2-12 with the as-drawn fact and ask for the maximum flowline pressure.

challenges.row_ref: 3 Reverse Flow - P-002 stops with wells lined up
challenges.challenge: Likelihood 3 is too low. P-002 stops at the end of every flushing job with flowlines lined up. Overpressure of the low-pressure side needs no flow, only seepage past one untested check valve and the pump valves into a section boxed in by the P-003 discharge check, the closed 2"-150# return valve and the hoses. There is no relief on the low-pressure side, and the only barriers are manual valve sequencing.
challenges.proposed_change: Rank current and residual People C4 / Env D4 / Asset D4 / Rep D4 (RR2) and keep the HOLD. State in remarks that the row cannot be reduced by R2-21 (procedure) alone. Reduction requires the protection specified under R2-19 to be installed.

challenges.row_ref: 10 Low Level - V-312 pumped down (and 1 No/Less Flow loss of suction)
challenges.challenge: Residual C2 credits R2-14 (LSLL-1004 at 300 mm stops P-003 and the burner). On 041 the suction nozzle is N4, the 2" '(NITROGEN CONN)' on the shell. It is drawn at the level of N13 (TT-1003), apart from the bottom nozzles (N2 and the 3" bottom connection), with a 4" leg dimensioned 1000 mm dropping from it. The P&ID is not to scale, so the elevation is unknown (H2-09). A nitrogen connection is not normally a bottom nozzle, though. If N4 is above 300 or 400 mm the pump loses suction before the L alarm or LL trip, and the trip is worthless. The 300 mm setting is a legacy value, not derived for this duty. TT-1003 would also read vapour at low level.
challenges.proposed_change: Row 10 residual: People C3 / Env E3 / Asset D3 / Rep D3 until N4 elevation is confirmed. Reword R2-14: 'trip level to be set from R2-17 (N4 elevation plus submergence for a 2" nozzle without vortex breaker); do not reuse 300 mm'. Add to R2-17: 'state usable batch volume between maximum pre-heat level and the trip, and evaluate taking suction from a bottom nozzle instead of N4'. Add to H2-09: 'elevations of N4 and N13 relative to the LL/L settings'.

challenges.row_ref: 7 High Temperature - burner over-firing
challenges.challenge: Residual C2 rests on R2-02 and R2-29. For R2-02 it is unknown whether the Murphy high-temperature switch senses heater outlet or an engine temperature. R2-29 is a trip from TT-1003, which measures tank bulk temperature on the shell at N13. That lags the heater outlet by the whole tank inventory and reads vapour if the level is below N13. The fast variable is heater outlet temperature, and the only device there is local TI-527 on 8097-H. 062 Note 5 gives 75-80 degC as a limit on gas evolution, which is set by outlet temperature, not bulk temperature.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R2-29: 'install an independent high-high temperature trip of burner fuel on the heater outlet (8097-H at the TI-527 location), with a high alarm; TT-1003 high alarm in addition'. Amend R2-02 to include 'confirm it senses heater outlet temperature'. Set residual People C3 / Env D3 / Asset D3 / Rep D3 until H2-07 confirms what the Murphy switch senses.

challenges.row_ref: 9 High Level - thermal expansion, gas swell and foaming
challenges.challenge: People severity D is inconsistent with Node 1 row 9.1. There, cold overfill from the same 3 m vent is ranked People C, with the conflict resolved as 'vent spray near fired unit'. Froth-over of crude at 75-80 degC with the burner firing is the worse case. Residual D2 also credits LSHH-1004, although the row itself notes a level switch may not see foam and its action is unknown.
challenges.proposed_change: Rank current People C4 / Env D4 / Asset D4 / Rep D4. Residual People C3 / Env D3 / Asset D3 / Rep D3: one step for the fill-level limit (R2-32) plus the burner trip (R2-33), with no severity change.

challenges.row_ref: 5 High Pressure - gas evolution exceeds 2" vent capacity
challenges.challenge: The row considers heat-up of a closed batch only. The basis does not state whether filling and heating are separated. In flushing mode the tank inventory is exported to the flowlines and must be made up. Opening the Node 1 feed (live crude saturated at separator pressure, 7 barg stated) into a tank already at 75-80 degC gives a far higher flash and foam rate than cold filling or closed-batch heating. Nothing limits the heating rate either: R2-30 fixes only the maximum temperature.
challenges.proposed_change: Add the cause 'live separator feed admitted to hot V-312 (make-up during recirculation or flushing)' to this row and to the High Level row. Add a parking-lot item to Operations / Process Engineering: 'Is make-up from V-301 / V-100 permitted while V-312 is hot or the heater is firing? Sequence of fill, stabilise, flush and refill?' Add to R2-26 the case 'live feed into hot tank'. Add to R2-30 'maximum heat-up rate / burner duty during stabilisation'. Add to R2-34 'Node 1 inlet 3"-150# valve closed and tagged before light-off unless make-up is specifically designed for'.

challenges.row_ref: 7 High Temperature - normal intent, sustained vapour release at the vent
challenges.challenge: The row is correctly held at residual = current, but the only actions are dispersion (R2-27), detection (R2-28) and evaluating a dip pipe (R2-57). The release is the design intent and lasts the whole stabilisation period. The source should be removed, not just detected. N11 already connects V-312 to the LAM-16 flare.
challenges.proposed_change: Cross-refer to the Node 1 recommendation to evaluate stabilising on the LAM-16 flare via N11 in place of the cold vent, and list it first in this row's rec_ids. Add to remarks: 'if the flare route is adopted, re-rank with likelihood reduced; if not, R2-27 must demonstrate no flammable concentration at the HOU burner and engine intake for the maximum evolution rate from R2-26'.

challenges.row_ref: 5 High Pressure - P-002 run against a closed well or header valve
challenges.challenge: The consequence is limited to the chiksan and 2" discharge. On 062, P-002 delivers into D013 flowlines that carry PSHH/PSLL pilots (for example PSHH-001A/PSLL-001B, 003A/B, 004A/B, 005A/B, 007A/B). Injection with the flowline blocked or restricted downstream raises flowline pressure. That either trips the producing well on PSHH (an unplanned shut-in during the job) or, if the pilots are isolated or defective, takes the flowline to the PD pump stall pressure. P-002's maximum pressure against the D013 rating is unknown.
challenges.proposed_change: Add to the consequence: 'flowline pressurised by P-002: well trip on flowline PSHH, or flowline overpressure if P-002 maximum pressure exceeds the D013 limit'. Add to H2-12: 'P-002 maximum discharge pressure against the D013 flowline rating and the flowline PSHH settings; status of the flowline pilots'. Amend R2-25: 'P-002 relief set at or below the lowest-rated item downstream (chiksan, 2"-DF/HD-D013 header, flowlines)'. Keep residual = current.

challenges.row_ref: 4. Mis-directed Flow - 4.3 Another V-301 inlet opened or passing (BV-018 HP header, BV-019, 4"-PR-D013-090-X, 6494-H/6498-H) + R1-19
challenges.challenge: On 031 every inlet to V-301 arrives through nozzle N20: BV-019 (drawn 6" NC) fed from BV-018 'FROM HP HEADER' and from 4"-PR-D013-090-X 'FROM 6" HEADER / FROM LAM-B/C COFLEX LINES', plus the green 6",600# valve from 6"-PR-D013-6498-H. Row 4.3 treats all of them as 'other' inlets and R1-19 blinds BV-018, BV-019, the coflex line and the LP separator gas lines. That leaves V-301 with no feed. Nobody has stated by which route well 192B reaches V-301 (or V-100). An operator cannot write a line-up sheet from this, and the blind list as written cannot be executed.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot item H1-25 (Client/Operations): 'By which header and valves does well 192B reach V-301 and V-100 during the trial; are the separators fed in parallel or one after the other; which other wells share that header; BV-019 is marked NC on 031.' Reword 4.3 cause to 'an inlet other than the designated feed route opened or passing, or another well opened onto the designated feed header by the production crew'. Reword R1-19 to 'every connection except the designated feed route (to be named once H1-25 is answered)'. Mark 4.3 HOLD with residual = current until the feed route is named.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING (12. Start-up / Shutdown - planned stop of transfer with wells still flowing)
challenges.challenge: Rows 1.2 and 12.2 cover a valve left closed by mistake and a handover. Neither covers the planned stop that happens on every batch: V-312 full, ST-017 taken out for cleaning (single basket, so transfer must stop), or the tank switched to heating. The well keeps flowing into the separators. With LV-303 bypass (017), 4"-PR-C013-155-X and 6"-PR-C013-152-X closed (client answer 12) and blinded under R1-19, and BV-396 / trunkline routes closed on 030, the separators have no liquid outlet. The operator must then either shut in the well, or re-open a normal production route in a hurry (a blinded route cannot be re-opened), or crack the strainer bypass, or keep filling a full tank. This is the most likely route to separator overfill and to the short-cuts listed in 19.2.
challenges.proposed_change: Add row 12.4 'Planned stop of transfer (tank full, strainer cleaning, change to heating mode) with well 192B still flowing and no alternative liquid route'. Consequences as 1.2 (separator overfill to LAM-16 flare) plus pressure to continue filling V-312 (9.1) or open the LC bypass (4.6). Safeguards: none defined, V-301 LSHH NOT CREDITED. Rank People D5, Env E5, Asset E5, Rep E4 as 1.2; residual = current, HOLD. Add parking-lot item H1-26 (Client/Operations): 'State of well 192B and of each separator between batches and during strainer cleaning: well shut in at choke/wing valve, or separator liquid returned to which normal route?' Amend R1-27 to state the stop sequence (well shut in or diverted and confirmed BEFORE the tank inlet or strainer valves are closed). Amend R1-19 so the designated alternative liquid route is valve-isolated and locked, not blinded.

challenges.row_ref: 9. High Level - 9.1 V-312 overfilled from Node 1 + 12.3 Emergency during transfer; R1-16
challenges.challenge: R1-16 puts the automatic stop at the V-312 end (fail-closed valve on 8085-H closed by LSHH-1004 / PSD-232). Closing the tank inlet while both separators are still dumping creates exactly rows 5.1 and 1.2: the 150# section (8083/8086/8087/8085-H and ST-017) settles out at source pressure with no relief, and the separators overfill because their own LSHH is dead. Residual C3 in 9.1 and C2 in 12.3 is taken without counting this. Also, on 041 the minimum-flow line 2"-PR-B013-8094-H joins 8085-H between the 3"-150# valve and N1; a shutdown valve placed on the tank side of that tee would dead-head P-003 on a high-level trip.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R1-16: LSHH-1004 / PSD-232 and the emergency stop push button shall close the source-side shutdown valves at the separator liquid outlets (the valves required by R1-03 and R1-15, upstream of the C013|B013 and D013|B013 breaks) first; any valve added on 8085-H shall be upstream of the 8094-H tie-in and shall not be the only final element. Add to remarks of 9.1 and 12.3: 'trip at tank end alone converts overfill into 5.1 / 1.2'. Keep residual of 9.1 and 12.3 = current (HOLD) until the final element location is fixed and R1-01 covers the blocked-in case.

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - 5.3 Gas blow-by from V-100; R1-18
challenges.challenge: The V-301 manual bypass (017) is listed as a blow-by cause in 5.2 and car-sealed by R1-18. The V-100 manual bypasses drawn on 030 are not: globe valves (019)/(020) around LV-102B on 2"-PR-D013-106, and valve (005) on 3"-PR-D013-102-E40 around LV-101B. LV-102B is severely corroded and LC-101B has a damaged gauge, so operating V-100 on a hand bypass is the realistic field response. A hand bypass left open with the level gone is a direct gas path through TP-02A/B or TP-01A/B into the 150# line and V-312, and no level valve refurbishment stops it.
challenges.proposed_change: Add to 5.3 cause: 'or manual bypass (019)/(020) around LV-102B or (005) around LV-101B opened by the operator (hand control of a defective valve, or to speed up the dump)'. Extend R1-18 to car-seal closed (019), (020) and (005) with entry in the locked-valve register, and add to R1-27: 'no operation of either separator on a manual bypass; if a level valve does not control, the transfer is stopped'.

challenges.row_ref: 1. No / Less Flow - 1.2 Line-up error (and 1.1 ST-017 plugged): residual ranking
challenges.challenge: 1.2 drops from D5 to D3 and 1.1 from D4 to D3 on R1-05, R1-06, R1-25 and R1-27. R1-05 allows the LSHH to 'stop inflow to V-301 OR alarm at a manned point'. No inlet shutdown valve is drawn on 031, LCP-002 has never been in service and its lamps are dead, and no manned point has been defined (H1-11, H1-19). R1-25 is a local DP gauge with no alarm and R1-27 is a procedure. A local alarm nobody is stationed at, a gauge and a line-up sheet do not justify two likelihood steps under the study's own ranking rule.
challenges.proposed_change: Delete 'or alarms at a manned point' from R1-05 and require a defined executive action (final element to be named by Instrumentation under H1-11). Until that final element exists on the P&ID, rank residual of 1.2 as D4 / E4 / E4 / E4 (one step, for the independent second-person check of the line-up in R1-27) and 1.1 residual = current, and mark both rows HOLD.

challenges.row_ref: 12. Start-up / Shutdown - 12.2 End of batch / shift change; 13. Loss of Utilities - 13.3 Loss of lighting / radio
challenges.challenge: Both rows state their consequence as 'overfill or blow-by' of V-312, but are ranked People D4. The same outcomes are ranked People C in 9.1 (C4) and 5.2 (C5) by team decision (c). The severity must follow the consequence, not the cause. In addition 13.3 takes a likelihood step from R1-27 alone; a procedure does not light a level gauge at night or give two operators at stations on three P&ID sheets a way to talk.
challenges.proposed_change: Re-rank 12.2 and 13.3 People C4 (Asset D4, Rep D4 as 9.1). For 13.3 add a new recommendation R1-46 (Operations): 'Provide certified temporary lighting at LG-301, the V-100 level gauge, ST-017, LG-1004 and the vent valves, and hazardous-area-rated radios with a dedicated channel for each station; transfer is stopped on loss of contact.' Without R1-46, 13.3 residual = current.

challenges.row_ref: 16. Drainage - 16.2 V-001 overfill; 9. High Level - 9.2 (P-116A/B via 2"-PR-B013-7917-H); R1-19
challenges.challenge: R1-19 blinds 'the V-001 pump line 7917', while 16.2 relies on P-116A/B being available to empty V-001 (4 m3, LG-001 only), which now also receives liquid carried through the common vent. The two rows contradict each other. Also, on 041 line 7917 does not enter V-312 directly: it joins the 6" bottom-outlet header through a 2"-150# check valve and a 3" valve marked LO, and that header reaches V-312 only through BV-358 (6",600#, clouded NC) at N2; the same header runs to 6"-PR-D013-2423-X 'TO TRITAN PUMP, QUINTPLEX PUMPS & TRIPLE PUMP-2'. With BV-358 closed for the campaign, where V-001 liquid goes is not shown.
challenges.proposed_change: Remove line 7917 from the R1-19 blind list. Correct 9.2 to say 'V-001 pump discharge reaches V-312 only if BV-358 is open or passing'. Add parking-lot item H1-27 (Operations/Engineering): 'Where is V-001 pumped during the campaign with BV-358 closed, and who watches LG-001?' Reference H1-27 in 16.2 and keep 16.2 residual = current (HOLD).

challenges.row_ref: 3. Reverse Flow - 3.3 Back-pressure of common vent into V-001; H1-16
challenges.challenge: The facilitator notes sheet 025 was not re-checked. On 025 the tie-in TP-12A/B is a tee, through a 2"-150# valve, off the existing V-001 vent line 2"-VA-B013-203-X, which continues up from nozzle N2 to its own hatched vent tip and carries the 'HOLD 1' flag. So V-001 does keep its own vent, and with the 2"-150# valve open V-312 vent gas or carried-over crude can come out of that second tip as well as going into the drum. Its height and location are not given. V-001 also receives 2"-PR-B013-097-X from the V-100 sheet (030) and the pig receiver / header drains, so other crews' draining and venting share the stack.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword 3.3 consequence: 'vapour or liquid from V-312 discharged at the existing V-001 vent tip (2"-VA-B013-203-X, height and location not stated) as well as into V-001'. Reword H1-16: drop 'whether V-001 keeps an independent vent' and ask instead for the height/location of the existing V-001 vent tip and the intended position of the 2"-150# valve at TP-12A/B. Extend R1-22 to treat the V-001 tip as a second release point. Add to R1-27: no draining or venting to V-001 by other crews while V-312 is filling or heating, unless the TP-12 valve position is defined.

challenges.row_ref: 17. Maintenance - 17.1 Routine basket cleaning on a single strainer; R1-28
challenges.challenge: Checked on 031: the 100% bypass 8087-H has one valve only (the LC 3"-150# at its inlet end) and its return leg ties into 8085-H downstream of the strainer outlet valve with no valve. So the section between the strainer outlet valve and the 3"-150# valve at V-312 is exposed to both separators through that single LC valve, and there is no bleed on that section (PI-54X is inside the strainer envelope, PI-549 is on the tank side of the V-312 valve on 041). R1-28 asks for isolation at TP-04 / TP-01A/B and at the tank but gives no way to prove it, and it says 'transfer stopped' without saying what the flowing well does meanwhile.
challenges.proposed_change: Amend R1-28: (a) well shut in or diverted and confirmed before isolation (cross-refer new row 12.4); (b) 3"-300# valve at TP-04 and 3"-600# valve at TP-01A/B closed and locked, PI-545 and PI-543 bled to zero and watched for build-up for a stated time before the cover vent is opened; (c) LC bypass valve confirmed closed and locked, key with the supervisor. Add new recommendation R1-47 (Process Engineering): 'Add a valved, plugged bleed between the ST-017 outlet valve / bypass return and the 3"-150# valve on 8085-H at V-312 so the downstream isolation can be proven.' Add to 17.1 safeguards: 'bypass return leg unvalved - outlet side isolation from the separators is one LC valve plus the outlet valve'.

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - 5.4 V-312 vent path closed or restricted (safeguard 2: PG-1004, PI-549)
challenges.challenge: PG-1004 is listed as a tank pressure indication during filling. On 041 it sits on the TP-05 return header, upstream of the 2",150# valve and the 3",600# BV-XXX at N6. During a cold fill, before recirculation is lined up, those valves may be shut and PG-1004 then reads nothing of the tank. The only gauge that is on the tank during a Node 1 fill is PI-549 (on 8085-H, tank side of the 3"-150# valve), and it is a new instrument whose location relative to the fill operator is not stated.
challenges.proposed_change: In 5.4 (and 5.2 safeguard 5, 4.2 safeguard 2) change PG-1004 to 'PG-1004 - reads tank pressure only when the N6 valves are open; NOT CREDITED during filling'. In R1-27 name PI-549 as the tank pressure reading to be logged during filling and require the N6 valves' position to be stated on the line-up sheet. No change to ranking.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING (parking lot - batch sequence and manning across Node 1 and Node 2)
challenges.challenge: The worksheets assume both a batch operation (fill, then heat, then flush) and, in Node 2 row 9, continued Node 1 inflow during recirculation. Nobody has said which it is. If live crude is topped up while the tank is recirculating or while P-002 is pumping to wells, the 'stabilised' batch is re-gassed and the vent load is fill flash gas plus heating gas at once. It also sets the crew: R1-27 needs a person at V-301, V-100 and V-312; Node 2 needs the HOU panel, P-003 LCP by the tank and, in flushing mode, the wellhead - six stations if run together. 062 Note 3 says well fluid flows from the test separator OR the Repco separator and 030 Note 7 says the test separator is used only if free water separation is required, while the client answer is both at the same time.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot item H1-28 / H2-26 (Client/Operations): 'Is V-312 filled, isolated from the separators, then heated and flushed (strict batch), or topped up during recirculation / flushing? Total crew available per phase. Reconcile client answer 2 (both separators together) with 062 Note 3 (OR) and 030 Note 7.' Interim basis: concurrent filling and heating treated as credible. Add to R1-27 and R2-34: separator feed valves at TP-04 and TP-01A/B closed and tagged before the burner is lit, unless the concurrent case is included in R1-22 / R2-27 and manned. Add to Node 2 row '11. Composition - crude declared stabilised' the cause 'Node 1 feed re-opened or passing into the stabilised batch'.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING (4. Mis-directed Flow - other V-312 liquid outlets)
challenges.challenge: Node 2 mis-directed flow covers the diesel line, the unheated hose route, TP-11 and TP-05, but not the tank's other liquid outlets on 041: N2 through BV-358 (6",600#, clouded NC) to the 6" header and 6"-PR-D013-2423-X 'TO TRITAN PUMP, QUINTPLEX PUMPS & TRIPLE PUMP-2' and the hose 'TO GENTEX PUMP'; and the bottom outlet through BV-359 (4",300#, clouded NC) to 3"-DC-B013-2404-X and 4"-PR-B013-3875-H 'TO LP INTERIM BULLET TANK HEADER'. These are the routes operators normally use to empty this tank. Left open or passing, hot gassy crude goes to pumps and a tank outside the trial, and V-312 level falls unnoticed until P-003 loses suction with the burner firing. The Node 1 blind list (R1-19) covers inlets only.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a Node 2 row under 4. Mis-directed Flow: 'BV-358 or BV-359 (or the 2" valve at N2) open or passing during heating / flushing'. Consequences: hot crude at up to 75-80 degC (per 062 Note 5) to the Tritan / Quintplex / Gentex pump suctions and the LP interim bullet tank header; unobserved loss of level leading to the low-level row. Safeguards: NC clouds (Note 7) - procedural; LSLL-1004 NOT CREDITED. Rank D4 / E4 / E4 / E4; residual D3 / E3 / E3 / E3 with a new recommendation R2-58 (Operations): 'Lock closed and tag BV-358, BV-359 and the 2" valve at N2 for the campaign, entered in the lock register, unless one is named as the water draw-off route.'

challenges.row_ref: 11. Part of - Composition - Free water heel and sand/solids in V-312 bottom; R2-31
challenges.challenge: R2-31 makes 'draining of free water from V-312 and the suction leg, confirmed by sample' a signed hold point, and the row credits 'local drain on suction leg and tank drain'. On 041 the pump suction is nozzle N4 on the head ('2" (NITROGEN CONN)'), part-way up the vessel, with the 4" leg dimensioned 1000 MM and its 2"-150# 'LOCAL DRAIN' hanging off N4. That drain only removes what comes over at N4 level; it cannot remove a water heel lying below N4. The true bottom outlets are the NC-clouded BV-358 / BV-359 routes into other systems. So the operator has no defined way to do what R2-31 asks, and the heel below N4 stays in the tank under a hot return.
challenges.proposed_change: Change the safeguard to 'Local drain on N4 leg - does not drain the tank heel; tank bottom drain route not defined - NOT CREDITED'. Split R2-31: (a) Process Engineering to name the water draw-off nozzle, route, destination and sample point for V-312 and show it on 041; (b) Operations to make the draw-off a signed hold point before light-off. Add parking-lot item H2-27: 'Which nozzle and route is used to draw free water from V-312 and where does it go; elevation of N4 above the vessel bottom (links H2-09).' Until (a) is answered, residual of this row and of the froth-over consequence in '7. High Temperature - burner over-firing' stays HOLD for the water part.

challenges.row_ref: 1. No / Less Flow - P-003 stops or trips while the burner keeps firing; R2-15
challenges.challenge: The row is written for recirculation mode. In flushing mode the engine-driven PD pump P-002 sits downstream of the heater (2" valve at TP-11). If P-003 stops (its only stop/start is the LCP at the pump by V-312, on electrical supply) the HOU engine, burner and P-002 keep running and P-002 goes on pulling through the coil and the feed hose from a dead centrifugal pump: suction falls, hot crude flashes in the coil, the hose can collapse, P-002 vapour-locks and hammers the chiksan line. R2-15 trips burner fuel only.
challenges.proposed_change: Add to the cause: 'in flushing mode P-002 continues to draw through the heater and hose after P-003 stops'. Add to consequences: 'coil and hose pulled below vapour pressure, hose collapse, P-002 vapour lock and pulsation on chiksan discharge'. Extend R2-15 to stop P-002 as well as burner fuel on P-003 not running, and state in R2-34 the manual sequence (burner off, P-002 stopped, well valve closed) for a P-003 stop. No change to ranking.

challenges.row_ref: 8. Low Temperature - Crude cools in 2" lines, hoses, pump and coil between batches or after burner trip
challenges.challenge: Residual E3 / E4 is taken on R2-34 and R2-35 only. Neither gives the crew any means of getting waxy crude out of the coil, the untraced hoses, the 3" line and P-003 before it sets. R2-22 spades the diesel supply at TP-10A, which is the only fluid on the drawing that could displace crude from the coil at the end of a job. The realistic outcome on a cold restart is what the row already describes: dead-head, flanges broken, external heat applied. A procedure with no method is not a likelihood reduction.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot item H2-28 (Operations/Process Engineering): 'How are the heater coil, hoses, P-003 and the new 2" lines emptied or displaced at the end of each batch and at the end of the campaign (with what fluid, to where), and how is the unit returned to diesel service?' Add to R2-34: end-of-batch displacement step once H2-28 is answered, and a ban on external heating or breaking flanges on a suspected wax plug without a permit. Keep residual = current (HOLD) until then. Note in R2-22 that the diesel spade must not remove the only displacement fluid without an alternative being named.

challenges.row_ref: 19. Any Other Safety Issue - Long recirculation left unattended or run at night; R2-50
challenges.challenge: R2-50 is timed 'During operation' and says 'restrict the trial to daylight until the trips are proven'. Under R2-01 to R2-08 there is no firing on crude at all before the trips are proven, so as written the daylight restriction never applies and night firing is allowed from the first batch, with the engine LCP work lights reported non-functional. It also does not say how many people or where; P-003's only stop is at the tank and the burner panel is at the HOU.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R2-50 (timing: Before start-up for the rule, During operation for the log): 'Minimum two persons while firing - one at the HOU panel, one at V-312 / P-003 LCP, in radio contact; a third at the wellhead in flushing mode; no firing unattended; daylight only for a stated number of first batches and thereafter only when R2-12 lighting and lighting at LG-1004 and the vent are in place; fixed-interval log as listed.' Reference H2-20 for the crew number.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING (parking lot - destination of flush returns; 'HOT INLET/OUTLET' label at N7B)
challenges.challenge: Two things on the drawings are not explained and the crew will ask on day one. (1) 062 shows the flush going to wells 120, 134LS/SS, 136LS/SS and 137LS/SS, and 031 Note 2 speaks of 'heating of stabilized crude oil from flushing operation'. Where the hot crude and what it brings back goes after the well is not stated; the well 120/137 manifold lines on 041 run back into the V-312 inlet header (6"-PR-B013-6698-X at BV-352), which Node 1 wants closed or blinded. (2) On 041 the lower level-bridle nozzle N7B carries the label 'HOT INLET/OUTLET' beside its 2",300# LO valve. If hot oil was ever meant to pass by that nozzle, the bridle carrying LSLL / LG / LT / LSHH-1004 is affected.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot item H2-29 (Client/Operations): 'Where do flush returns from the flushed well go, and do they come back to V-312 or V-301 during the campaign?' with interim basis 'returns not routed to V-312; manifold inlets at BV-352 closed'. Add to H2-11: 'meaning of the label HOT INLET/OUTLET at N7B on 041 and whether the level bridle shares a nozzle with any hot connection'. Reference H2-29 in the row '4. Mis-directed Flow - mode change-over error at TP-11A/B' and in '11. Composition - crude declared stabilised'.

challenges.row_ref: 5.2 Gas blow-by from V-301 (also 1.1, 1.2) - safeguard 1 wording; R1-03 / R1-04
challenges.challenge: Row 5.2 says the V-301 LSLL is 'not independent of LV-303'. On 031 the sensors are independent: LSHH-304 is on its own nozzles N13/N14 (valves 140/141) and LSLL-305 on N15/N16 (142/143), while LIC-302 and LG-301 share a separate standpipe off N18 (145). What is missing is any final element or signal line: nothing is drawn from either switch, there is no shutdown valve on the V-301 liquid outlet or inlet, and LCP-002 is not on the drawing at all. As written, R1-03 (new independent trip) and R1-04 (replace existing LSLL) overlap and it is not clear whether one or two sensors are intended.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword safeguard: 'LSLL-305 sensor on dedicated nozzles N15/N16 (independent of LIC-302 bridle) - NOT CREDITED: cable disconnected, no final element or logic drawn'. Merge the intent: R1-04 (Maintenance) reinstates the LSLL switch as the sensor; R1-03 (Instrumentation) provides the logic and a dedicated fail-closed shutdown valve upstream of TP-04 (upstream of the C013|B013 break and of the (017) bypass return, otherwise the bypass defeats it). State in R1-03 that the trip must not pass through LCP-002 unless the LCP is proven (never in service).

challenges.challenge: 031 shows the bottoms of the LSHH-304 chamber, the LSLL-305 chamber and the LIC-302/LG-301 standpipe all tied to one common line running to the N12 side; only the standpipe leg has a valve (a new 1/2" drawn in the proposed colour). No valve is drawn on the two switch legs. If this is a common drain header without isolation on the switch legs, the three devices are hydraulically cross-connected (sludge/wax common cause; wet-testing one switch disturbs the controller and the other switch). The team cannot tell from the drawing.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot item (Instrumentation / Operations): 'Function of the common bottom line joining LSHH-304, LSLL-305 chambers and the LIC-302 standpipe on 031; are there drain valves on the switch legs in the field; where does it drain?' Interim basis: independence of the switches from the control bridle NOT CREDITED until confirmed. Reference it in 5.2 and 17.3 and add 'flush each chamber and prove independent wet test' to R1-14.

challenges.row_ref: 1.1 / 1.2 V-100 safeguards; 5.3 V-100 blow-by; H1-12
challenges.challenge: The V-100 level instrumentation is under-described. 030 shows three switches on one external bridle off N4/N5 (valves 001/002): LSHH-101B, LSH-101B and LSLL-101B, together with LG-102B; a second gauge LG-102A and an untagged 'LLC' controller sit on a separate standpipe. No signal line or final element is drawn from any of the three switches, and none of them is on the inspection sheet. The draft omits LSH-101B, treats 'the V-100 level gauge' as a single item (the sheet does not say whether LG-102A or LG-102B is the corroded one), and the sheet's 'LC-101B' does not appear on 030 (drawing shows 'LLC' and an untagged dashed-signal instrument at LV-101B).
challenges.proposed_change: In 1.1, 1.2 and 5.3 list 'LSHH-101B / LSH-101B / LSLL-101B on one common bridle (N4/N5) with LG-102B - hardware, NOT CREDITED (not inspected, no final element drawn, common-cause blockage)'. Extend H1-12: which gauge (LG-102A or LG-102B) is corroded; what LSH-101B does; which controller is LC-101B on the drawing. Amend R1-15 to require the new V-100 LSLL trip sensor to be function-tested by wet test of the bridle and its final element located upstream of the D013|B013 break at TP-01A/B.

challenges.challenge: The draft names LV-102B as a principal blow-by initiator and SAFETY CRITICAL for the oil route. On 030, LV-102B is a 1" valve (2"x1" reducers) on 2"-PR-D013-106 whose outlet goes to TP-02A/B (the free-water route of Note 3), while the oil outlet 3"-PR-D013-102-E40 is controlled by LV-101B (2" valve, FIT-102C downstream), with LCV-304 (2",600#, FI-101) tying in downstream of FIT-102C. LV-101B does not appear by tag on the inspection sheet; the sheet has an untagged valve '910091-010' (good condition) that may or may not be it. So the valve most likely to pass oil/gas to TP-01A/B has NO known condition, and the corroded LV-102B is on the highlighted TP-02 path.
