challenges.proposed_change: Rewrite cause 5.3: '(a) LV-101B on oil outlet 102-E40 fails open - condition unknown, not identifiable on inspection sheet; (b) LV-102B (1", water outlet to TP-02A/B, severely corroded) fails open or leaks; (c) LCV-304 (reported good)'. Add to H1-12: 'Is untagged valve 910091-010 the P&ID LV-101B? As-found condition of LV-101B.' Add a recommendation (Maintenance): inspect, tag and stroke-test LV-101B before start-up; keep R1-10 for LV-102B but state it is on the TP-02A/B route.

challenges.row_ref: 2.1 / 2.2 More Flow and 9.1 V-312 overfill - 'no flow measurement'
challenges.challenge: The statement 'None instrumented - no flow measurement' is true for the new 3" line and for V-301 but not for V-100: 030 shows FIT-102C on the oil outlet downstream of LV-101B and FI-101 on the LCV-304 line, and the V-100 sheet reports '2 flow meters' and the 'Barton chart & flow transmitter' in good condition and operating. Which two meters were inspected, and where FIT-102C reads/totalises, is not stated.
challenges.proposed_change: In 2.2 and 9.1 add safeguard 'FIT-102C / FI-101 on V-100 oil outlet (030), reported good - procedural only (readout location and totaliser not confirmed; does not see V-301 flow or the TP-02A/B water route)'. Add parking-lot question: 'Which two flow meters were inspected on V-100, where do they indicate/totalise, and can they be used for batch accounting?' No change to ranking. Add to R1-27 that V-100 batch volume is logged from the totaliser if confirmed; V-301 contribution remains unmetered.

challenges.row_ref: 9.1 V-312 overfill; 5.1 blocked outlet; 1.2; R1-16
challenges.challenge: R1-16 puts the LSHH-1004/PSD-232 shutdown valve 'on 8085-H at V-312'. (1) Closing a valve at the tank end with both separators still feeding creates exactly the 5.1 scenario (150# B013 section and ST-017 boxed in at source pressure, no relief) and the 1.2 scenario (separator level rise with dead LSHH) on every high-level trip. (2) On 041 the P-003 minimum-flow line 8094-H joins 8085-H between the 3"-150# valve and N1; a valve placed downstream of that tie-in would also dead-head the pump recycle. (3) The trip sensor shares the single bridle N7A/N7B (valves marked LO) with LT-1004, LG-1004 and LSLL-1004, so the alarm, the gauge and the trip have one common-cause failure.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R1-16: 'PSD-232 (LSHH-1004) and the emergency stop shall close the source shutdown valves required by R1-03 (V-301, upstream of TP-04) and R1-15 (V-100, upstream of TP-01A/B); any additional valve on 8085-H shall be upstream of the 8094-H tie-in and shall not be the only final element.' Add recommendation (Instrumentation): provide the high-level trip or the pre-alarm from a sensor independent of the N7A/N7B bridle (041 shows 4" nozzles N14 and N15 unused) - to be evaluated. Add 'trip of R1-16 as a cause of blocked-in B013 section' to row 5.1 causes.

challenges.row_ref: 9.1 V-312 overfill - safeguard 2 (LT-1004) and H1-09
challenges.challenge: 041 prints H 2000 / L 400 mm but draws no alarm function for them: LT-1004 is a plain field bubble with no signal line, no LI/LAH/LAL; only LSHH-1004 and LSLL-1004 have shared-display symbols with PSD-232 / PSD-231. So a 'high level alarm at 2000 mm' does not exist on the drawing, and R1-17 ('inspect, calibrate, function-test') cannot create one. The 9.1 residual (C4 to C3) partly leans on operator warning before the trip.
challenges.proposed_change: State in 9.1: 'H 2000 / L 400 settings have no alarm instrument drawn (LT-1004 has no output shown) - no pre-alarm exists'. Add recommendation (Instrumentation): provide an audible/visible high level alarm from LT-1004 at the tank and at the filling operator's position (separators), set from the maximum fill level in R1-27/R2-32. Extend H1-09: 'Is PSD-231/232 logic in a live plant PSD system, and where are LSHH/LSLL-1004 annunciated?'

challenges.row_ref: 1.2 Line-up error / separator overfill - residual D5 to D3; R1-05, R1-06
challenges.challenge: Residual drops two likelihood steps on R1-05 (replace LSHH and test 'to a defined action that stops inflow to V-301 or alarms at a manned point'), R1-06 (restore LCP-002) and a procedure. 031 shows no automatic valve on any V-301 inlet (BV-018, BV-019 are manual) and no logic; LCP-002 has never been in service and what it shuts is unknown (H1-11). Maintenance can replace a switch and lamps but cannot define a final element that does not exist; 'or alarms' is an escape clause. The reduction is therefore not backed by a real barrier.
challenges.proposed_change: Split R1-05: (a) Maintenance - replace and reconnect LSHH-304; (b) new recommendation, Instrumentation - define and install the LSHH executive action (close an automatic inlet valve to V-301 or shut in the feeding well) with cause-and-effect, and function-test; delete 'or alarms at a manned point'. Until (b) is defined, residual for 1.2 = D4/E4/E4/E4 (procedure and gauge only) with HOLD on H1-11. Same treatment for row 12.3, whose residual credits LCP-002 functions that are unknown.

challenges.row_ref: 13.1 Instrument air failure; 5.6 PV-303; R1-32
challenges.challenge: R1-32 instructs 'set the level valves to fail closed' and the row assumes PV-303 fails closed, without the actuator action being known; 031/030 show no fail-position legend on LV-303, PV-303, LV-101B, LV-102B, LCV-304 or PLV-100B, no PIC is drawn for PV-303 at all, and no signal line links LIC-302 to LV-303. The motive medium for the V-301 pneumatic controllers (instrument air or instrument gas) is not shown; only V-100 has an 'instrument air manifold' on its sheet. Changing actuator action is a design change (spring/actuator swap), not a setting, and a fail-closed PV on a separator whose only relief is an uncertified PSV-304A raises 5.6.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R1-32: 'Verify in the field and mark on 030/031 the supply medium and air-failure action of each valve; Process/Instrumentation to specify the required action (level valves closed; pressure valve action decided against the PSV-304A/B status) and Maintenance to convert where different.' Add to H1-10: 'Is the V-301 controller supply instrument air or separator gas; where is the PV-303 pressure controller sensed and what is its set point?' Add PSV-304B reinstatement (R1-09) as a precondition in 13.1 remarks.

challenges.row_ref: 5.2 / 5.3 residual C5 to C3 and R1-02 V-312 relief device
challenges.challenge: The two-step likelihood reduction relies on new LSLL trips (R1-03, R1-15) whose final elements do not exist, whose logic solver is undefined and whose integrity target has not been set, plus a PSV whose sizing is on HOLD. With the initiating valve reported defective (demand rate high) a single new, simple, switch-based trip does not justify two decades without a SIL determination; no recommendation asks for one.
challenges.proposed_change: Add recommendation (Instrumentation): 'Carry out a LOPA/SIL determination for the V-301 and V-100 low-low level trips and the V-312 high-high level trip, and specify proof-test interval, bypass control and independence from the BPCS accordingly.' Show residual for 5.2/5.3 as C4 (one step for the restored/refurbished control loop and trip as specified) with remark 'further reduction to L3 conditional on LOPA result and R1-02 sizing - HOLD'.

challenges.row_ref: 3.3 / 16.2 common vent with V-001; H1-16
challenges.challenge: H1-16 asks 'whether V-001 keeps an independent vent'. Sheet 025 answers it: the existing V-001 vent 2"-VA-B013-203-X from N2 continues past TP-12A/B up to its own tip device (HOLD 1 flag on that riser), and the new 2"-150# valve ties that riser to the new cold vent. So V-312 vent gas and carry-over can leave through the existing V-001 stack tip as well, and into V-001 where the vent/drain headers from sheets 021-024, 030 and 032 terminate. V-001 has LG-001 only - no level switch or alarm - and P-116A/B are air-driven with manual start.
challenges.proposed_change: Correct 3.3 and H1-16 wording: 'V-001 retains its own vent stack (2"-VA-B013-203-X, tip location and height not given); the TP-12 valve cross-connects the two vents'. Add the V-001 stack tip as a second release point in R1-22 and R1-45 (area classification). In 16.2 safeguards state 'no level alarm or switch on V-001' and add recommendation: 2"-150# valve at TP-12 kept closed and locked during V-312 open-vent operation unless R1-22 shows the cross-tie is required.

challenges.row_ref: 1. No/Less Flow - P-003 stops / valve closed with burner firing (rows 1 and 2); R2-01; H2-07
challenges.challenge: The condition report calls the device a 'heater low-flow indication switch' - it may only drive an indication, not a burner trip. Separately, 062 shows the existing P-001 delivering into H-001 inside the skid, while crude now enters through BV-001 with P-001 bypassed. The location of the low-flow sensor, the low-pressure Murphy switch and any 'centrifugal pump running' permissive relative to the BV-001 entry is unknown: if they sit on the P-001 circuit they are outside the crude path, or they hold the burner out until the non-functional alarm bypass switch is used. Replacing the switch (R2-01) then restores nothing, yet the residual is taken from C4 to C2.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot item (Instrumentation / HOU vendor): 'Where are the low-flow switch, low-pressure switch and any P-001 run permissive physically located relative to BV-001, and does each one trip burner fuel or only indicate? Can the burner fire with P-001 stopped without using the alarm bypass?' Change R2-54 from 'flow indicator' to 'install a flow transmitter/switch on the heater inlet downstream of TP-10 with a hard-wired low-low flow trip of burner fuel, independent of the existing HOU switch'. Residual for rows 1 and 2: C3 (new trip + R2-15) with HOLD on the new parking-lot item; C2 only after the cause-and-effect of R2-52 is confirmed.

challenges.row_ref: 7. High Temperature - burner over-firing; 5. heater blocked in; R2-02; R2-29
challenges.challenge: The 'Murphy high-temperature switch with gauge' is assumed to be the heater outlet temperature trip. The report does not say what it measures; on an engine-driven unit it could equally be engine coolant temperature (the same panel has a 'coolant overheat' lamp). R2-29 then takes the independent high-high trip from TT-1003, which on 041 is on tank nozzle N13 and feeds a shared-display TIA-1003 with a LOW alarm only: it measures tank bulk temperature, lags the coil outlet by the whole tank inventory, sees nothing if the return is blocked or the line-up is to P-002, and has no drawn link to the stand-alone HOU burner panel.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot question: 'What does each Murphy switch-gauge sense (heater outlet, engine coolant, engine oil, P-001 discharge)?' Reword R2-29: 'Install an independent high-high temperature trip on the heater outlet (at TP-11A/B, upstream of the mode valves; TI-527 on 8097-H is local indication only and is bypassed in flushing mode), hard-wired to burner fuel shut-off; add a high alarm on TIA-1003 for tank bulk temperature (froth-over warning).' Residual of the over-firing row: C3 with HOLD until the function of the existing switch is confirmed.

challenges.row_ref: 12. Emergency at HOU - ESD inoperable; 15. engine ingestion; R2-04, R2-05, R2-46
challenges.challenge: R2-04 says 'prove that the ESD button shuts down the burner'. The only ESD action evidenced in the condition report is the emergency air shut-off valve (which failed to respond from both LCPs); whether ESD also closes burner fuel is not known. The HOU ESD has no drawn link to P-003, whose only stop is the START/STOP LCP at the pump on 041, so a working HOU ESD still leaves the electric pump feeding a hose or coil leak. Whether the engine has an automatic overspeed trip onto the air shut-off valve (the real protection against gas ingestion, independent of a push button) is also unknown.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R2-04/R2-05 into one cause-and-effect requirement: 'ESD from either LCP and from the remote station (R2-46) shall close burner fuel, close the engine air shut-off valve and stop P-003; prove each output by witnessed test.' Add parking-lot question: 'Does ESD shut burner fuel; is there an engine overspeed trip acting on the air shut-off valve?' Amend R2-28: gas detection at the engine air intake to act directly on the air shut-off valve and burner fuel, not alarm only. Keep the 12/15 residuals but mark HOLD on the ESD cause-and-effect.

challenges.row_ref: 6. Low Pressure - hose burst; R2-03
challenges.challenge: Residual C4 to C2 credits the Murphy low-pressure switch after replacement, but its function is unconfirmed (remark itself says 'if it is the process loss-of-feed trip'); it may be an engine oil-pressure device. A low-pressure switch also cannot distinguish a hose burst from normal low back-pressure when the heater discharges to an atmospheric tank, so even a process switch may never see a trip condition in recirculation mode.
challenges.proposed_change: Residual C3/E3/D3/D3, crediting only R2-36 (hard pipe or certified hose) - HOLD on H2-07 for any further credit. Add to R2-03: 'Process Engineering to confirm that a usable low-pressure trip point exists between normal operating pressure in recirculation mode and the burst case; if not, rely on the low-flow trip of R2-54.'

challenges.row_ref: 2. More Flow - P-002 rate / speed regulators; 7. over-firing cause; R2-09
challenges.challenge: The draft assumes both malfunctioning 'speed regulators' control P-002 / engine speed and classes them 'safety related'. The report lists two regulators without saying what each regulates (engine governor, P-002 drive, P-001 drive, burner blower/fuel). If one governs the burner air/fuel or the engine that drives it, it is an initiating cause of over-firing or flame-out, i.e. part of a preventive barrier. The 'Centrifugal On/Off switch - functioning normally' (P-001) is also not addressed: P-001 is bypassed but can still be started from the panel.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot question: 'What does each speed regulator control, and is burner firing rate dependent on either?' Until answered, class R2-09 as SAFETY CRITICAL (initiator of 7. High Temperature and 2. More Flow) and list it in the session notes with the other critical defects. Add to R2-23: 'electrically lock off the P-001 centrifugal switch for the crude campaign and confirm no burner permissive depends on it.'

challenges.row_ref: 10. Low Level in V-312; 1. loss of suction; R2-14
challenges.challenge: R2-14 wires LSLL-1004/PSD-231 (300 mm) to stop P-003 and the burner and the residual falls to C2. P-003 on 041 has only a local START/STOP LCP - no starter interface, run status or trip input is drawn - and PSD-231 is a function of an existing shared-display system whose present outputs are unknown (likely tied to the tank's former export duty). LSLL shares the bridle with LG/LT, which the cause itself says can be wax-plugged. N4 elevation versus 300 mm is unknown, so the switch may act after the suction is already uncovered.
challenges.proposed_change: Extend R2-14: 'Provide P-003 starter with a hard-wired trip input and run-status contact; burner fuel to trip first/simultaneously (R2-15); set point of the low-low trip to be fixed from the R2-17 NPSH result and N4 elevation, raising it above 300 mm if required; bridle flushing connection and heat tracing confirmed.' Add to H2-11: 'What do PSD-231/232 currently trip, and will those existing actions cause unwanted shutdowns elsewhere when V-312 is dedicated?' Residual C3 until set point and independence from the common bridle are confirmed (HOLD H2-09, H2-11).

challenges.row_ref: 8. Low Temperature - flame-out / relight; 12. Start-up - burner light-off
challenges.challenge: Both rows are ranked L3 as found while every other row with no working protection is L4. As found, the flame reset button is damaged, the status lamps are dead, the alarm bypass switch is in an unknown state, the LCP internals are extensively corroded and flame detection/purge logic is unknown; repeated manual relight attempts are the expected behaviour. L3 ('unlikely') is inconsistent with the stated ranking basis.
challenges.proposed_change: Current risk for both rows: People C4, Asset D4, Reputation D4 (Environment unchanged). Row 8 residual stays = current (HOLD H2-07). Row 12 residual C3/D3/D3, not C2, until R2-52 confirms a flame-failure fuel shut-off and purge sequence actually exists - mark HOLD H2-07.

challenges.row_ref: 9. High Level - thermal swell / foaming; R2-33
challenges.challenge: R2-33 configures LSHH-1004/PSD-232 to shut burner fuel, and the residual falls two steps (D4 to D2). The same switch is asked in Node 1 (R1-16) to close the fill valves; neither recommendation mentions the other, the switch is on the shared N7A/N7B bridle, a float/displacer switch may not respond to foam (the draft says so), and stopping the burner does not stop continued inflow from the Node 1 feed, P-116A/B or LCV-1005 (FO), which are listed causes.
challenges.proposed_change: Combine into one PSD-232 cause-and-effect entry referenced from both nodes: 'LSHH-1004 closes Node 1 source shutdown valves AND trips burner fuel; P-003 keeps circulating'. Add a high alarm ahead of the trip (see Node 1 LT-1004 alarm item). Residual D3/D3/E3/D3 (one step), with remark that foam response of the level switch type is unverified - add to H2-11: 'type of LSHH-1004 (float, displacer, other) and its suitability for foaming hot crude'.

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - 5.1 Blocked outlet of the 150# B013 section (also 9.1 / 12.3 via R1-16)
challenges.challenge: R1-16 puts a fail-closed shutdown valve on 3"-PR-B013-8085-H at V-312. Every trip of that valve boxes in the Class 150 section (8083-H, 8086-H, ST-017, 8087-H, 8085-H) against both separators through the open 3"-300# (TP-04) and 3"-600# (TP-01A/B) valves. That is exactly cause 5.1, now on automatic demand, and the section has no relief and a strainer of unknown rating. R1-24 (new check valve on 8085-H) adds another liquid-lockable section. Row 5.1 itself rests only on the study R1-01, so no physical barrier is defined.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R1-16 so the shutdown valve(s) sit on the HP side of the spec breaks (C013 at TP-04, D013 at TP-01A/B), or make R1-16 conditional on the measure below. Add a new Mechanical/Integrity + Process recommendation to 5.1: EITHER rate everything from TP-04 and TP-01A/B up to and including the last block valve before V-312 (3"-150# on 8085-H), including ST-017 and bypass 8087-H, for the upstream class (spec break moved to the last valve), OR fit a full-flow PSV on the B013 section. Add the R1-24 check valve section to the R1-26 TSV list. Keep 5.1 residual = current until one option is selected.

challenges.row_ref: 12. Start-up/Shutdown - 12.1 First hydrocarbon into new piping and ex-stock strainer (also 5.1, 17.1; R1-29, H1-04)
challenges.challenge: ST-017 is ex-stock (031 Note 3) with design pressure not available (client answer 6), and there is no inspection sheet for it. R1-29 tells us to pressure-test ST-017 'to the line class test pressure'. Testing a vessel of unknown rating to a B013 test pressure can itself damage or fail it. Nothing requires the strainer's own condition to be established (body and cover thickness, cover gasket and bolting, basket, drain valve). It is a pressure boundary taking flow from 300#/600# sources.
challenges.proposed_change: Split R1-29. (a) Lines: test as written. (b) New recommendation, Mechanical/Integrity, before start-up, flagged SAFETY CRITICAL pressure boundary: do not install ST-017 until nameplate / data sheet / material certificate are produced; inspect internally and externally, measure thickness, renew cover gasket and bolting, check basket; hydrotest only to the strainer's own documented test pressure. If no documentation exists or the rating is below the governing pressure from R1-01, reject it and procure a strainer rated for the section. Keep 12.1 residual at C3 (HOLD on H1-04) until (b) is closed.

challenges.row_ref: 17. Maintenance - 17.2 PSV-304B removed (also 1.2, 5.6; R1-09, H1-02)
challenges.challenge: On 031 both PSV outlets (3"-PR-B013-149-X) reach the flare line only through 3"-PR-C013-148-X and the 3" valve (100), which joins the 6" line downstream of FSV-003. A second 3" valve (105) sits at the top of 149-X with an open flanged end drawn above it. The row and R1-09 name only (013)/(014)/(015)/(016). If (100) is closed, both PSVs are isolated regardless of those four valves. If (105) is open or unblinded, relief and flare gas discharge locally at V-301. Also the PSV inlet header is labelled 2"-PR-C013-114-X while the break flag at each PSV reads D013|B013.
challenges.proposed_change: Add valves (100) and (105) to cause 17.2 and to the PSV-304A NOT CREDITED statements in 1.2 / 5.6. Extend R1-09: lock open (100), close and blind the open end at (105), blank the vacant PSV-304B inlet and outlet flanges until it is refitted. Extend H1-02: as-found position of (100) and (105), purpose of the open end at (105), and the correct class of the PSV inlet (C013 vs D013).

challenges.row_ref: MISSING
challenges.challenge: Deviation 18 has no row for the integrity of V-312 itself, although the vessel is inside Node 1. No inspection sheet exists for it. The service changes to repeated heating to 75-80 degC (per P&ID note), an air-breathing open vent and possible water heel. The inspection sheets for neighbouring equipment report severe external corrosion. H1-03 asks for 'last inspection' only as a data question. The same gap applies to existing parts re-used as boundaries: N10 2",600# vent valve, nozzle valves, the bridle off N7A/N7B (2",300# LO valves) and the existing header from TP-05 to N6.
challenges.proposed_change: Add row 18.3: 'V-312 shell, heads, nozzles, supports, bridle and re-used existing valves/lines - as-found condition not reported; internal corrosion from air/water on open-vent hot service; external corrosion / CUI'. Consequence: leak or nozzle failure of a tank holding hot crude, pool fire. Safeguards: none evidenced. Rank on the same basis as 18.1 and hold residual = current until the record exists. New recommendation, Mechanical/Integrity, before start-up: produce the V-312 nameplate data and a current inspection record (external visual, UT thickness of shell / heads / nozzles, support and earthing check, bridle and nozzle valve condition) and confirm fitness for the new temperature.

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - 5.2 Gas blow-by from V-301 (also 5.3, 5.4; H1-03, H1-20)
challenges.challenge: The rows assume the V-312 shell is the element that fails ('vessel assumed unable to withstand source pressure'). The drawing does not support or deny that. What 041 does show is that existing V-312 nozzle valves are called out 600# / 300# (N5, N6, N10, N11 at 600#; N7A/B 2",300#; BV-359 4",300#), while every new attachment is B013 with 150# valves: 8085-H at TP-06A, 8088-H at N4/TP-07 to ex-stock P-003, 8095-X at TP-08, 8097-H at TP-05. No spec-break flag is drawn at any of these tie-ins. If V-312 pressurises, the new 150# piping, the P-003 casing and seal (rating unknown) and the HOU hoses see tank pressure. The release may be at grade at the pump or HOU, not only at the vent.
challenges.proposed_change: Add to consequences of 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.4: 'pressure imposed through open N4 / N6 / N1 on 8088-H, P-003 casing and seal, 8097-H and HOU hoses - release at grade at pump or HOU'. Extend R1-01 scope to these items. Extend H1-03 / H1-20: V-312 nameplate design pressure against the 600#/300# nozzle valve callouts, and where the spec breaks are at TP-05, TP-06A, TP-07 and TP-08 (none drawn).

challenges.row_ref: 4. Mis-directed Flow - 4.5 V-100 routing (also 5.1; H1-23)
challenges.challenge: On 030 the second use of 3"-PR-B013-8087-H (at TP-02A/B, with PI-544) is a line labelled class B013 fitted with a 2"-600# check valve and 2"-600# valve. It connects the V-100 outlet piping 2"-PR-D013-106-E40 to the D013 route at TP-03 / 4"-PR-D013-5076-X (LLP header). No spec break is drawn at either end. As drawn it is a 150#-class line number between two D013 systems. The worksheet treats it only as a duplicate line number.
challenges.proposed_change: Add this section to cause 5.1 and to R1-01 as a possible under-rated section. Add to H1-23 / H1-20: is the TP-02A/B to TP-03 line B013 or D013, and where are its spec breaks. Add to R1-36 the correction of its number and class.

challenges.row_ref: 3. Reverse Flow - 3.3 Back-pressure on common vent (also 16.2; H1-16)
challenges.challenge: The facilitator did not check sheet 025. It shows TP-12A/B on the existing V-001 vent riser 2"-VA-B013-203-X, which continues upward to its own tip device and carries the 'HOLD 1' flag. The new 2"-150# valve leads off 'TO NEW COLD VENT'. So V-001 (4 m3 vent/drain drum) does keep its own vent, and the two vents are interconnected. 041 labels the same connector 'VENT FROM EXISTING OPEN DRAIN TANK'. V-312 vent gas therefore has a second outlet at the V-001 stack, and HOLD 1 on 025 applies to that existing riser.
challenges.proposed_change: Correct 3.3 and 16.2: V-001 has its own vent riser 203-X; cross-flow is in both directions; the V-001 stack is a second release point for V-312 gas or liquid. Reword H1-16: delete 'whether V-001 keeps an independent vent'; ask instead for the height and location of the V-001 stack, the trial position of the TP-12 2"-150# valve, and why the tie is needed. Add the V-001 stack as a release point in R1-22 and R1-45.

challenges.row_ref: 17. Maintenance - 17.1 Routine basket cleaning on a single strainer
challenges.challenge: Residual D3 rests on a procedure (R1-28) and one check valve (R1-24). The task is frequent, done by hand on a body fed from 300#/600# sources through single 150# block valves, with a 100% bypass that can stay live alongside. A procedure alone is weak support for a likelihood step. The row also omits the 1/2" valved connection drawn between the inlet block valve and the strainer on 031, so the available bleed points are understated.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a physical recommendation, Mechanical/Integrity, before start-up: provide positive isolation at ST-017 for cleaning - spectacle blinds at inlet and outlet flanges, or a second block valve each side with the existing 1/2" connections used as proven bleeds - and a pressure gauge on the strainer body. Correct safeguards to list the 1/2" connection upstream of the basket. Residual D3 only with this hardware; otherwise keep D4.

challenges.row_ref: 2. More Flow - 2.1 LV-303 passing / wide open (slugging and vibration)
challenges.challenge: The consequence names slugging and vibration of the new 3" line and the 1/2" DBB branches. None of the four recommendations on the row (R1-07, R1-14, R1-18, R1-27) addresses pipe support or small-bore connections. The line carries flashing two-phase flow by design, and blow-by gas in upset. The 1/2" branches at PI-545, PI-543, PI-54X, PI-549 and the strainer cover vent are unbraced cantilevers as drawn.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a recommendation, Mechanical/Integrity, before start-up: design and check supports and guides of 8083/8085/8086-H for two-phase slug loads, brace or shorten all 1/2" DBB / vent / drain branches, and walk the line for vibration during the first transfer as a hold point. Attach it to 2.1, 2.2 and 5.2.

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - 5.4 V-312 vent path closed or restricted (also 8.2; R1-22)
challenges.challenge: The vent 2"-VF-B013-8095-X is an untraced '-X' line. It rises from N10, runs horizontally past the 8096-X branch and ends in a free-standing stack marked '3 METERS APPROX'. R1-22 is a process calculation. Nobody owns the mechanical design of the vent: slope and absence of pockets where condensate or wax can sit, support of the stack against wind and against the reaction of a gas/liquid slug (the row itself predicts a slug), and thermal growth when hot vapour flows in Node 2.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a recommendation, Mechanical/Integrity, before start-up: route 8095-X free-draining back to V-312 with no pockets (or a valved, plugged low-point drain), design the stack support for wind and discharge reaction, and include it in the flexibility check. Reference it in 5.4, 8.2 and 9.1.

challenges.row_ref: 7. High Temperature - 7.1 Heat tracing control failure (also 15.2; H1-15)
challenges.challenge: The tracing is credited as 'present' on client answer 8, but its type is unknown. If it is electric, it is new electrical equipment inside the zone of the strainer, drains and vent. Its certification and maximum sheath temperature are not covered by 15.2 or H1-15. R1-42 gives 'commissioning' to Maintenance although the tracing is new construction with no specification.
challenges.proposed_change: Extend H1-15: electric or other, hazardous-area certification and temperature class, power source. Add tracing to the equipment list in R1-45. Change R1-42 owner to the party installing the new lines, with Maintenance witnessing.

challenges.row_ref: 4. Mis-directed Flow - 4.1 V-301 liquid header routes (H1-13)
challenges.challenge: The line is 4"-PR-C013-155-X on 031 but arrives on 041 as 4"-PR-D013-155X3 'FROM REPCO SEPARATOR' with connector 032-00, not 031-00. It joins the N5 collector through a 4"x3" reducer with no valve of its own on 041. The only valve before N5 is the common 3",600# BV-XXX (NC), shared with 3"-PR-D013-WH193X2-X. The piping class changes between sheets with no spec break shown.
challenges.proposed_change: Quote both line numbers in 4.1. Add to H1-13 / H1-23: class of line 155 (C013 or D013) and the intermediate sheet 032. State in R1-19 that the blind for this route must be at the V-301 end, because the N5 valve is common with the WH 193 CHP line.

challenges.row_ref: 18. Corrosion/Erosion - 18.1 As-found external corrosion (R1-10, R1-07)
challenges.challenge: R1-08 and R1-11 include a body thickness check, but R1-10 (LV-102B, 'severe corrosion on both valve body and stem') and R1-07 (LV-303) do not. No recommendation states an acceptance criterion or a pressure test after refurbishment. 'Refurbish' could be closed by painting. Residual D3 depends on restored pressure boundary, not appearance.
challenges.proposed_change: Amend R1-07, R1-08, R1-10 and R1-11 to one standard: measure body wall against minimum required thickness, renew stem / packing / bolting, shell and seat pressure-test after overhaul, signed record; replace the valve if below minimum. Keep 18.1 residual at D4 for any valve returned without a test record.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING
challenges.challenge: No row asks whether ex-stock P-003 can do the duty of the bypassed HOU booster pump P-001. The 041 data box gives 34 m differential head. The pump must push through 2" lines, a 2"x1" discharge reducer, the hose, 4" BV-001, the heater coil of unknown pressure drop, and up to top nozzle N6. If the system resistance is higher than the pump can meet, coil flow is permanently low with the burner firing. This is a design cause of Less Flow, not an upset. The low-flow switch set point also belongs to the old diesel / P-001 duty.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a row under 1. No/Less Flow: 'P-003 head/capacity inadequate against coil + hose + line resistance - sustained low coil flow'. Consequence as the first row (coil overheating), ranked the same. Recommendations: (new, Process Engineering with Mechanical, before start-up) system curve against the P-003 curve at the heater's minimum coil flow; set the low-flow trip (R2-01) from that figure; add R2-54 flow indicator. Residual = current, HOLD on H2-07, H2-08, H2-10.

challenges.row_ref: 1. No/Less Flow - Loss of pump suction (H2-08, R2-17)
challenges.challenge: 041 draws a 2"x1.5" reducer at the pump suction and 2"x1" at the discharge, with a 2" suction line from a 2" nozzle (N4). The data box lists 25/20/13 m3/h. On nominal bores (pipe schedule not given) 25 m3/h is roughly 3 m/s in the 2" suction line and about 5 m/s in a 1.5" nozzle, and above 10 m/s in a 1" nozzle. Either the data box does not describe the pump actually in stock, or the suction is undersized for bubble-point hot crude with possible sand.
challenges.proposed_change: Add to H2-08: actual suction / discharge nozzle sizes of the pump in stock and which capacity applies. Extend R2-17 to include suction line sizing and reducer orientation (eccentric, flat side up), not NPSH alone. Keep the row at residual = current.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING
challenges.challenge: Mechanical seal leakage of P-003 appears only as a secondary effect of cavitation or dead-heading. There is no row for the seal as a cause in normal running: ex-stock pump with aged elastomers, hot volatile crude at 75-80 degC (per P&ID note) near bubble point, sand, seal type unknown. The pump sits beside V-312 with a motor and LCP of unknown Ex rating. R2-39 inspects the pump but does not require a seal suited to the service.
challenges.proposed_change: Add row under 18 (or 19): 'P-003 seal / casing joint leak in normal operation'. Consequence: hot crude spray or pool at the pump, fire under V-312. Safeguards: none evidenced. Rank People C4 on the same basis as the hose-burst row. Extend R2-39 / R2-18: fit a new seal and elastomers confirmed suitable for hot volatile crude with solids, provide a drip tray to a contained drain, coupling guard. Residual likelihood reduced only when the seal specification is confirmed.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING
challenges.challenge: At TP-05 the new B013 line 8097-H joins an existing header through a 2",600# valve. That header also carries LCV-1005 (FO) and its 2",600# bypass from 2"-PR-D013-5037-X 'centrifugal pump recycle line/PSV'. The existing row ranks only mis-direction (E4). It does not consider that the D013 source can pressurise 8097-H, the heater outlet, the coil and the hoses when the path to N6 is shut (2",150# valve or 3",600# BV-XXX) with the TP-05 valve open. No spec break is drawn at TP-05.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a High Pressure row: 'Pressure from 5037-X / LCV-1005 imposed on Class 150 line 8097-H, heater and hoses with N6 route closed'. Rank on the conservative basis that the D013 source exceeds Class 150; residual = current, HOLD on H2-16. Add TP-05 to the R2-19 HP/LP review. Add to H2-16: maximum pressure in 5037-X.

challenges.row_ref: 6. Low Pressure - Feed hose bursts (R2-36) and 7. High Temperature - thermal growth (R2-42)
challenges.challenge: R2-36 offers 'replace the heater feed hose with hard piping'. The hose is also the only flexible element between fixed plant piping and the engine-driven, vibrating HOU skid, and it absorbs thermal growth of the 2"/3" feed. Hard piping without a designed flexible element moves the failure to the skid nozzle or BV-001 flange. R2-36 and R2-42 conflict as written. R2-42 also covers only the new 2" lines, not the existing 3" feed, the heater outlet to TP-11 or the tank end of 8085-H that sees the hot minimum-flow return.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R2-36: certified, pressure-tested metallic flexible hose (conductive, whip-restrained) rated for maximum heater temperature and pump shut-off pressure, or hard pipe with a designed flexible / vibration-isolating element. Extend R2-42 to the 3" feed, heater outlet / TP-11 tee, 8094-H / 8085-H at TP-06A and vent 8095-X, and to include skid vibration and bracing of the 1/2" PI-551 branch and the TI-527 thermowell.

challenges.row_ref: 18. Corrosion/Erosion - Heater coil condition unknown
challenges.challenge: Residual drops two likelihood steps (C4 to C2) on R2-38, a one-off thickness and pressure test of a coil whose design pressure, design temperature and material are unknown (H2-07). The test pressure cannot be set without that data. One inspection does not control in-service fouling, coking or sand erosion on the new crude duty.
challenges.proposed_change: Set residual to C3 with HOLD on H2-07. Reword R2-38: obtain coil design data first; test to the coil's documented test pressure and confirm it covers P-003 shut-off and the TP-11 HP/LP case from R2-19; repeat thickness check after the first campaign.

challenges.row_ref: 12. Start-up/Shutdown - First crude service of untested new lines and ex-stock pump
challenges.challenge: People is ranked D4 for a leak at a new joint, hose coupling or pump seal 'near burner, fire'. The same outcome is ranked C4 in the hose-burst row and C3 in the Node 1 first-fill row. A leak ignited at a manned fired unit is the same consequence whichever joint fails.
challenges.proposed_change: Change current to People C4 (Asset D4, Reputation D4). Residual C2 only on signed test records from R2-38 / R2-39 / R2-40; otherwise C3.

challenges.row_ref: 17. Maintenance - Work on P-003 seal or suction strainer
challenges.challenge: The row says 'single-valve isolation from hot V-312'. On 041 the suction has two 2"-150# valves in series: one at N4 (TP-07) and one near the pump. Between them is the 4" leg with its 2"-150# LOCAL DRAIN. That gives a usable double block and bleed on the tank side. The single isolations are on the discharge side: check valve + 2"-150# valve to the HOU, and check valve + valve on 8094-H.
challenges.proposed_change: Correct the cause and safeguards: tank side has two block valves with the leg drain as bleed (procedural); the HOU and minimum-flow sides are single valve plus check. Make R2-56 require both suction valves closed with the leg drain proven. Add a bleed point or blind on the discharge side.

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - P-002 run against a closed valve (also 2. More Flow - P-002 rate; R2-09)
challenges.challenge: Both HOU speed regulators are reported malfunctioning. The worksheet classes them 'safety related' and links R2-09 only to the More Flow row. P-002 is a positive displacement pump whose own relief valve is not shown and not confirmed (H2-12). Until that relief is proven, speed control is the only thing limiting P-002 rate and pressure, and it is defective. The report does not say which machines the two regulators control.
challenges.proposed_change: Class the speed regulators SAFETY CRITICAL until the P-002 relief valve is confirmed and tested. Add 'speed regulator malfunction' as a cause in the P-002 High Pressure row and add R2-09 to that row. Add a parking-lot item: which drive each of the two regulators controls, and whether an overspeed trip exists.

challenges.row_ref: 4. Mis-directed Flow - Unheated route / bypassed booster pump P-001 (R2-23, H2-14)
challenges.challenge: The condition report lists a 'Centrifugal On/Off switch - functioning normally'. If that switch drives the bypassed booster pump P-001, the pump can still be started from the panel while connected to the filter pot and the heater inlet. The row covers only valves and hoses. What the switch drives is not stated in the report or on 062.
challenges.proposed_change: Add to H2-14: what the 'Centrifugal On/Off' switch drives. If it is P-001, add to R2-23: lock off and tag the switch / drive for the crude campaign and blank the P-001 discharge connection to the heater.

challenges.row_ref: MISSING
challenges.challenge: 041 carries the text 'HOT INLET/OUTLET' on the V-312 head beside nozzle N7B. Nothing in the worksheet refers to it. It is not clear whether it marks an existing nozzle, an internal heating element or an old annotation. Its isolation status is not shown. An unidentified connection on the tank that will hold hot crude cannot be left unexplained.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a parking-lot item to Engineering: what 'HOT INLET/OUTLET' on V-312 denotes, whether a nozzle or internal exists there, and its isolation / blanking status for the campaign. Reference it in row 4.2 and in R1-19.

challenges.row_ref: 3. Reverse Flow - 3.3 (common vent / V-001) and H1-16
challenges.challenge: Sheet 025 answers part of H1-16 and the row misses it. V-001 is drawn with its own existing vent 2"-VA-B013-203-X from N2 to an atmospheric terminal, with the HOLD 1 flag on that line. The new 2"-150# valve at TP-12A/B is a branch off that line 'TO NEW COLD VENT'. With the valve open there are two release points for V-312 gas: the 3 m vent and the V-001 terminal, whose height and location are not given. Sheet 025 also shows V-001 receiving streams unrelated to the trial: 3"-VF-B013-3870-X 'FROM LP PUMPS PSV OUTLET (P-105/106)', the drain from the 14" LAM-C pig receiver, 2"-PR-B013-097-X from sheet 030, and VF/DC headers from sheets 022/023/024/032. Those discharges could then emerge at the 3 m vent beside the HOU at any time.
challenges.proposed_change: Rewrite cause 3.3 to state the 025 facts. Add two consequences: (a) V-312 flash or blow-by gas released at the V-001 terminal on 203-X (unassessed location), and (b) PSV or drain discharges from other equipment released at the 3 m vent. Reword H1-16 to: 'Is the existing V-001 vent 203-X retained or removed, what is its terminal height and location, and what is the trial position of the TP-12 valve?' Add a recommendation (Operations): keep the 2"-150# valve on 8096-X locked closed for the campaign, provided Engineering confirms 203-X stays open as the V-001 vent. Extend R1-22 to cover both terminals. Keep residual = current (HOLD).

challenges.row_ref: 4. Mis-directed Flow - MISSING (TP-09 line to fuel gas conditioning skid)
challenges.challenge: On 041 the existing line from N10 runs to 'TO FUEL GAS CONDITIONING SKID' (049). The new open vent riser is teed into it at TP-08, and the only separation is one new manual valve at TP-09 with no NC or LC marking. Row 3.3 covers this in half a sentence ('gas exchanged with the TP-09 line') and does not rank it. It is a separate hazard: a fuel gas system connected to an open atmospheric vent and to an air-breathing tank through one unmarked valve.
challenges.proposed_change: Add a row under 4 Mis-directed Flow. Cause: TP-09 valve left open or passing. Consequences: (a) fuel gas back-flows and is released continuously from the 3 m vent near the HOU; (b) V-312 vapour, air or carried-over liquid enters the fuel gas conditioning skid and its consumers. Safeguards: single manual valve, procedural, position not defined. Rank People C4, Env E4, Asset D4, Rep D4, on the basis that fuel gas pressure and consumers are unknown. New recommendation (Operations): spade the TP-09 connection for the campaign and enter it on the blind register; residual C2 / E2 / D2 / D2. Add to R1-19 and to H1-16 (fuel gas pressure, and what N10 was used for before).

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - 5.2 / 5.3 (blow-by) and recommendation R1-02
challenges.challenge: The residual C3 rests on a V-312 relief device 'discharging to a safe location'. No safe location exists on the drawings: the atmospheric vent is on HOLD 1, and the only engineered disposal route, N11 to the LAM-16 flare (6"-VF-D013-6490-X via FSV-032), is closed by 041 Note 5 and R1-20. A PSV relieving blow-by gas to atmosphere beside the fired heater prevents vessel rupture but leaves the flash fire, which is the People C consequence in the row.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R1-02: 'Relief device to discharge to the LAM-16 flare header unless the R1-22 dispersion and radiation study demonstrates that atmospheric discharge of the full blow-by relief rate is acceptable at the HOU, engine intake and manned positions.' Add the PSV relief case to the R1-22 scope and to H1-03 (flare back-pressure, and whether FSV-032 is acceptable in a relief path). State in the remarks of 5.2 and 5.3 that residual C3 is claimed only for vessel rupture, and that the flash-fire consequence stays at current risk (HOLD) until R1-22 closes.

challenges.row_ref: 5.2 / 5.3 / 4.2 (Environment severity) and all rows using 'grade / ground / bund / vehicles'
challenges.challenge: The worksheet assumes an onshore plot throughout ('pool at grade', 'spill to ground / drains', 'vehicles', 'no bund'). No document supplied states whether LAM-28 is an offshore platform or an onshore site, so the spill receptor (deck and sea, or soil) is unknown. Environment is also ranked inconsistently: tank overfill (9.1) and blocked vent (5.4) are Env D, while loss of containment of V-312 itself in 5.2 / 5.3 and uncontrolled inflow in 4.2 are Env E.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot H1-25 (Client / HSE): 'Is LAM-28 offshore or onshore? Where do deck or area drains, the open drain tank and V-001 overflow discharge? Is there spill containment and oil spill response?' Affects every Environment ranking, 9.1, 16.1, 16.2 and H1-21. Interim basis: release can reach the sea or uncontained ground. Raise Environment to D in rows 5.2, 5.3 and 4.2 (D5, D5, D4), consistent with 9.1 and 5.4. Replace 'grade / ground / vehicles' with neutral wording ('deck or grade') until answered.

challenges.row_ref: 11. Composition - 11.1 (live crude, continuous flash gas) and 15. Ignition - 15.2
challenges.challenge: Residual credit is taken for R1-35 and R1-43. R1-35 is temporary or portable detection with an audible alarm only. R1-43 restores a manually initiated ESD. Neither removes the burner flame, which is a continuous ignition source, before a cloud arrives; an operator has to hear the alarm and reach a button inside the cloud. In 15.2 the two-step reduction from C3 to C2 also leans on R1-45, which is a sketch. Node 2 holds the same release at residual = current, so the two nodes disagree.
challenges.proposed_change: Reword R1-35 to require fixed (temporary-fixed is acceptable) point or line gas detectors between the vent and the HOU, at the engine air intake and at ST-017, with voted executive action: trip burner fuel, close the engine air shut-off, stop P-003 and close the source shutdown valves. Portable and personal monitors are additional only. Row 11.1: residual stays C4 / E4 / D4 / D4 (HOLD on R1-22 / H1-08) unless detection has executive action, then C3. Row 15.2: residual C3 at most, not C2, until the area classification and the separation distance (H1-19) are confirmed.

challenges.row_ref: 6. Low Pressure - 6.2 (air ingress) and 15. Ignition/Static - 15.1
challenges.challenge: As drawn, a flammable vapour space is the normal condition for every batch: open vent, no blanket, breathing on pump-down and cool-down, and live crude splash-filled at N1 immediately after a strainer (a charge generator with no relaxation length shown). No barrier exists, so L3 understates the likelihood compared with other no-barrier rows ranked L4. Row 15.1 then claims residual C2 from bonding (R1-34), a first-fill purge (R1-30) and the procedure. Bonding does not remove charge carried in the liquid or mist, and the purge is lost at the first pump-down. Row 6.2 is itself on HOLD for exactly this reason.
challenges.proposed_change: Rank 6.2 and 15.1 current People C4, Env E4, Asset D4, Rep D4. Hold 15.1 residual = current pending R1-31 and H1-24. Add a recommendation (Process Engineering): limit inlet velocity to 1 m/s until the N1 inlet is submerged, provide relaxation residence time downstream of ST-017 or a dip pipe, and confirm whether the vent tip device is a flame arrester. Add lightning or static ignition at the vent tip to the consequence text.

challenges.row_ref: 5. High Pressure - 5.5 (external pool fire under V-312 / ST-017)
challenges.challenge: The residual drops to C2 on R1-02 (PSV) and R1-37 (PSSR 'confirming fire-fighting in place'). A relief valve does not protect an unwetted shell in a pool fire and does not reduce fire likelihood. R1-37 is a confirmation, not a barrier. No fire water, foam, passive protection, containment or drainage is shown on any document.
challenges.proposed_change: Set residual = current (C3 / D3 / C3 / D3) and mark HOLD on H1-19 and H1-21. Add a recommendation (HSE): define and deploy fire protection for the V-312 / ST-017 / P-003 / HOU area before start-up, covering foam and cooling-water coverage with stated application rates and reach, spill containment or drainage that leads a pool away from under V-312, and remote isolation of feed. Residual may be re-ranked to C2 only after this is installed and R1-02 includes the fire case.

challenges.row_ref: 12. Start-up/Shutdown - 12.3 (emergency during transfer) and recommendation R1-16
challenges.challenge: R1-16 places the shutdown valve on 8085-H at V-312. Closing it on LSHH or emergency stop boxes in the Class 150 section and ST-017 against both separators, which is the unprotected blocked-outlet case 5.1 (HOLD). It also does nothing for a leak upstream of it, at ST-017 or at the TP-04 / TP-01 tie-ins. The residual C2 in 12.3 therefore rests on a valve in the wrong place and on manual initiation. Node 2 raises a separate remote stop (R2-46), so an operator would have two unrelated stop buttons in an emergency.
challenges.proposed_change: Amend R1-16: the emergency stop and LSHH-1004 / PSD-232 shall close the source shutdown valves upstream of the spec breaks (the R1-03 valve upstream of TP-04 and the R1-15 valve on the V-100 outlet). Any valve at V-312 is additional only. Make it one campaign emergency stop, operable from a safe location and from each manned station, which also trips P-003, burner fuel and the engine air shut-off (merge with R2-46). Change the 12.3 recommendation list to R1-03, R1-15, R1-16, R1-06, R1-27 and the residual to C3 / E3 / D3 / D3, because initiation is manual. Extend H1-19 with escape routes and muster point relative to the vent and HOU.

challenges.row_ref: Recommendation R1-22 (and its Node 2 duplicate R2-27)
challenges.challenge: The same HOLD 1 study is raised twice with different owners (R1-22 Process Engineering, R2-27 HSE) and different scopes. Neither includes the ignited cases. A vent tip about 3 m above the working level puts a jet or torch fire, flashback and liquid rain-out at head height for the operator at LG-1004, the P-003 LCP and the HOU panels.
challenges.proposed_change: Merge into one action with a split deliverable. Process Engineering: vent capacity, back-pressure and liquid carry-over for filling flash gas, heating gas evolution, blow-by and PSV relief. HSE / Technical Safety: unignited dispersion to LFL and 50% LFL at the burner, engine air intake, P-003 motor and manned positions; ignited vent thermal radiation contours; liquid rain-out footprint. Output to fix vent height and location, tip device, knock-out or liquid seal, and the exclusion zone. R2-27 becomes a cross-reference. Acceptance criteria to be stated in the action.

challenges.row_ref: 7. High Temperature - second row (normal recirculation, sustained vapour release from the 3 m vent)
challenges.challenge: This is an intended, continuous release for the whole stabilisation period of every batch. It comes from a vent about 3 m high, beside a naked-flame heater and a diesel engine whose ESD and air shut-off have failed on test, with no gas detection and no dispersion result. Node 1 ranks blow-by L5 because every layer is dead. The same reasoning applies here, with the release certain and not dependent on a failure. L4 is not defensible as found.
challenges.proposed_change: Rank current People C5, Asset D5, Rep D5 (Env stays E5), and state in the remarks 'no heating on crude until HOLD 1 is closed'. Residual stays equal to current (HOLD H2-03 / H2-06 / H2-18). Cross-reference the merged dispersion and radiation action.

challenges.row_ref: 15. Ignition/Static - second row (vapour reaches HOU burner / engine intake)
challenges.challenge: Residual C2 is claimed, while the release that feeds this row (dev 7, second row) is held at current risk. R2-05 restores an air shut-off that needs a manual ESD. R2-44 is a sketch. Nothing stops a diesel engine running away on ingested vapour before someone reacts. The condition report says only that the air shut-off did not respond to ESD; whether it has an automatic overspeed actuation is not stated.
challenges.proposed_change: Residual C3 / E3 / D3 / D3, conditional on R2-28 having executive action (burner fuel trip, engine air shut-off, P-003 stop). Add a recommendation (Maintenance / Mechanical): fit and test an automatic overspeed-actuated air intake shut-off and an exhaust spark arrestor on the HOU engine, and verify exhaust and firebox surface temperatures against the area classification. Add to H2-18: 'Does the existing emergency air shut-off close automatically on overspeed? Where is the engine air intake relative to the vent?'

challenges.row_ref: 9. High Level - thermal expansion / foaming, hot crude and foam ejected from the 3 m vent
challenges.challenge: People is ranked D4, but Node 1 ranks cold overfill from the same vent as People C (9.1, team decision c). Here the liquid is at up to 75-80 degC per the 062 note, ejected as spray and foam at about 3 m over people who are required to be at the tank and HOU, next to the burner. Hot overfill cannot be less severe than cold overfill. The residual D2 also rests on preventive actions only.
challenges.proposed_change: Rank current People C4, Env D4, Asset D4, Rep D4. Residual C3 / D3 / D3 / D3 (two preventive layers: fill limit R2-32 and LSHH burner trip R2-33; no severity change). Add a mitigation recommendation, linked to the vent study: a knock-out or liquid catch on the vent, or relocation of the discharge away from manned positions, and a marked exclusion zone under the vent during heating.

challenges.row_ref: 7. High Temperature - third row (hot surfaces) and recommendation R2-43
challenges.challenge: Personnel protection is considered only for the new lines, hoses and pump. Hot crude also fills existing equipment whose insulation status is not shown: the V-312 shell, the common level bridle and LG-1004 gauge glass (where R2-50 puts an operator at fixed intervals), the existing N6 header and '-X' lines tied to it, and the '-X' vent line 8095-X carrying hot vapour. A gauge glass failure with hot crude at operator face height is not recorded anywhere.
challenges.proposed_change: Add parking-lot H2-26 (Mechanical / HSE): 'Is V-312, its level bridle and LG-1004 and the existing connected piping insulated or guarded? What are the temperature rating and type of the LG-1004 gauge glass, and does it have excess-flow ball checks?' Extend R2-43 to these items. Add to the row consequences: 'gauge glass or bridle leak of hot crude at the reading position'. People stays E5 for contact burns; add D4 for the gauge-glass case until H2-26 is answered.

challenges.row_ref: 12. Start-up/Shutdown - second row (emergency at HOU or vent) and recommendations R2-46 / R2-51
challenges.challenge: R2-46 gives a remote stop for P-003 and the HOU only. In an emergency during recirculation the separators can still be feeding V-312 (Node 1), and V-312 inventory still gravity-feeds a leak through N4 / 8088-H because there is no remote isolation at the tank outlet. R2-51 asks for a response plan, but nothing defines escape routes, muster point or alarm communication for crew standing between the vent and the heater.
challenges.proposed_change: Merge R2-46 with the Node 1 emergency stop into one campaign ESD (source shutdown valves, P-003, burner fuel, engine air). Add a recommendation (Process Engineering / Instrumentation): a remotely operable or fire-safe fail-closed valve at the V-312 outlet N4 (TP-07), closed by the same ESD. Extend R2-51 to state escape routes and muster point clear of the vent plume and HOU, wind indication (windsock), and the means of raising the alarm. Residual C3 stays, but only with the N4 isolation; otherwise residual = current.
